data.htmlContent:
⚖️ 核心考点：前科弹劾
Impeachment by Prior Conviction (FRE 609)

本题考察的是《联邦证据规则》第609条关于使用刑事定罪记录来弹劾（质疑）证人可信度的规则，特别是关于时间限制的规定。

📖 法律规则解析
1. 涉及不诚实的犯罪 (Crimes of Dishonesty)
题目中被告的定罪是“伪造信贷申请”(falsifying a credit application)。这属于涉及不诚实或虚假陈述的犯罪（crimen falsi）。
根据 FRE 609(a)(2)，无论该犯罪是重罪(Felony)还是轻罪(Misdemeanor)，只要涉及不诚实，通常必须被法庭采纳用于弹劾，法官没有自由裁量权去排除它（除非太旧）。
2. 10年时间限制 (The 10-Year Rule)
这是本题的关键例外。
FRE 609(b) 规定： 如果从定罪或从监禁中释放（以较晚者为准）算起已经超过 10年，则该证据通常不可采纳。

除非满足极其严格的条件：证明价值(Probative Value) 实质性超过(Substantially Outweighs) 偏见性影响(Prejudicial Effect)。这在实践中很难满足。

✅ 正确答案分析：选项 D

“被告于12年前从监狱获释。”

这是拒绝该证据的最佳理由。

  • 计算时间：释放时间是12年前，已经超过了10年的门槛。
  • 法律后果：一旦超过10年，证据的推定状态变为“不可采纳”。
  • 举证责任倒置：检察官必须证明该证据的价值极高，且需提前书面通知。对于一般的弹劾目的，法院极有可能依据 FRE 609(b) 排除此证据。
❌ 为什么其他选项无效？
选项 A 定罪正在上诉中：
FRE 609(e) 明确规定，上诉并不影响定罪证据的可采性。
选项 B 是轻罪而非重罪：
对于“伪造信贷申请”这种涉及不诚实的犯罪，FRE 609(a)(2) 不区分重罪或轻罪，一律可采。
选项 C 被判缓刑而非监禁：
判罚的类型（缓刑 vs 监禁）本身不影响定罪记录的可采性。它只影响10年期限的起算点（从定罪日算起，因为没有监禁释放日）。
💡 MBE 解题技巧：
看到 Impeachment 题目，首先判断犯罪类型（是否涉及不诚实？），其次立刻检查时间（是否超过10年？）。
"Dishonesty" (不诚实) 犯罪通常是自动准入的，唯有 "Time" (时间) 是其最大的克星。

questions.question:
In a civil trial arising from a car accident at an intersection, the plaintiff testified on direct examination that he came to a full stop at the intersection. On cross-examination, the defendant's lawyer asked whether the plaintiff claimed to have been exercising due care at the time, and the plaintiff replied that he had been driving carefully. At a sidebar conference, the defendant's lawyer sought permission to ask the plaintiff about two accidents in the previous 12 months in which he had received traffic citations for failing to stop at stop signs. The plaintiff's lawyer has objected.
Should the court allow defense counsel to ask the plaintiff about the two prior accidents?

choices.a: No, because improperly failing to stop on the other occasions does not bear on the plaintiff's veracity and does not contradict his testimony in this case.
choices.b: No, because there is no indication that failing to stop on the other occasions led to convictions.
choices.c: Yes, because improperly failing to stop on the other occasions bears on the plaintiff's credibility, since he claims to have stopped in this case.
choices.d: Yes, because improperly failing to stop on the recent occasions tends to contradict the plaintiff's claim that he was driving carefully at the time he collided with the defendant.

data.questionStem:
Q87110

In a civil trial arising from a car accident at an intersection, the plaintiff testified on direct examination that he came to a full stop at the intersection. On cross-examination, the defendant's lawyer asked whether the plaintiff claimed to have been exercising due care at the time, and the plaintiff replied that he had been driving carefully. At a sidebar conference, the defendant's lawyer sought permission to ask the plaintiff about two accidents in the previous 12 months in which he had received traffic citations for failing to stop at stop signs. The plaintiff's lawyer has objected.

Should the court allow defense counsel to ask the plaintiff about the two prior accidents?

在一起因十字路口车祸引发的民事审判中，原告在直接询问中作证称，他在十字路口完全停了车。在交叉询问中，被告律师询问原告是否声称当时尽到了应有的注意义务，原告回答说他当时驾驶得很小心。在一次席边会议上，被告律师请求许可，询问原告关于其在过去12个月内发生的两起事故，在这两起事故中，他因未在停车标志前停车而收到交通罚单。原告律师对此提出了异议。

法院是否应允许被告律师就这两起先前的事故对原告进行提问？
options:
A. No, because improperly failing to stop on the other occasions does not bear on the plaintiff's veracity and does not contradict his testimony in this case.
不应允许，因为在其他场合未能正确停车的行为与原告的诚信无关，也与其在本案中的证词不矛盾。

B. No, because there is no indication that failing to stop on the other occasions led to convictions.
不应允许，因为没有迹象表明在其他场合未能停车的行为导致了定罪。

C. Yes, because improperly failing to stop on the other occasions bears on the plaintiff's credibility, since he claims to have stopped in this case.
应允许，因为在其他场合未能正确停车的行为关系到原告的可信度，因为他声称在本案中停了车。

D. Yes, because improperly failing to stop on the recent occasions tends to contradict the plaintiff's claim that he was driving carefully at the time he collided with the defendant.
应允许，因为近期未能正确停车的行为，倾向于反驳原告关于其与被告相撞时小心驾驶的主张。
data.explanation:
Methods of impeaching witness


MethodDescriptionMeans
Character for truthfulness
  • Reputation or opinion testimony
  • SIC involving bad act
  • SIC involving criminal conviction of felony or crime of dishonesty
  • Extrinsic evidence
  • Intrinsic evidence
Self-interest / biasMotive to lie or partiality to partyIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Prior inconsistent statementWitness's prior statement inconsistent with present testimonyIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Specific contradictionEvidence directly contradicting witness's testimony on material issueIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Sensory abilitiesEvidence showing witness's senses were impaired by physical / mental condition or environmental factorsIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
SIC = Specific instance of conduct.

Any party may impeach (ie, discredit) a witness by inquiring into specific instances of conduct (SICs) that bear on the character for truthfulness of (1) the witness or (2) another witness about whose character the witness being questioned has testified. And a witness can always be impeached with evidence that contradicts his/her testimony about an important issue in the case.

Here, defense counsel sought to ask the plaintiff about two prior accidents in which he had been cited for running stop signs. But these SICs do not bear on the plaintiff's truthfulness (ie, veracity) since running stop signs demonstrates carelessness - not dishonesty (Choice C). Nor do they contradict the plaintiff's testimony in this case since he did not claim that he has never run a stop sign (Choice D). Therefore, the court should not allow defense counsel to ask the plaintiff about the accidents.

(Choice B) Under Federal Rule of Evidence 608(b), a witness can be impeached with bad acts that did not result in criminal convictions. But the plaintiff's prior accidents remain inadmissible because they do not bear on truthfulness or contradict prior testimony.

Educational objective: A witness can be impeached with specific instances of conduct that bear upon truthfulness. And a witness can also be impeached with evidence that contradicts his/her testimony about an important issue in the case.

选项正确率统计：A选项 66%（正确选项），B选项 4%，C选项 15%，D选项 13%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

弹劾证人的方法


方法描述方式
诚信品格
  • 声誉或意见证词
  • 涉及不良行为的特定行为事例(SIC)
  • 涉及重罪或不诚实犯罪之刑事定罪的特定行为事例(SIC)
  • 外在证据
  • 内在证据
自身利益/偏见说谎的动机或对一方当事人的偏袒内在或外在证据
先前不一致的陈述证人先前与当前证词不一致的陈述内在或外在证据
具体矛盾在关键问题上直接反驳证人证词的证据内在或外在证据
感知能力显示证人感官因身体/精神状况或环境因素而受损的证据内在或外在证据
SIC = 特定行为事例。

任何一方当事人均可通过询问与以下人士的诚信品格相关的特定行为事例 (SICs) 来弹劾（即，质疑其可信度）证人：(1) 该证人，或 (2) 被询问的证人曾为其品格作证的另一名证人。此外，证人也随时可能被那些与其关于案件中重要问题的证词相矛盾的证据所弹劾。

在本案中，被告律师试图询问原告关于其因闯停车标志而被开罚单的两起先前事故。但这些特定行为事例与原告的诚信（即，诚实性）无关，因为闯停车标志表现的是粗心——而非不诚实（选项C）。这些事例也并未与原告在本案中的证词相矛盾，因为他并未声称自己从未闯过停车标志（选项D）。因此，法院不应允许被告律师就这些事故对原告进行提问。

（选项B）根据《Federal Rule of Evidence》第608(b)条，证人可以因未导致刑事定罪的不良行为而被弹劾。但是，原告先前的事故仍然不可采纳，因为它们与诚信无关，也与先前的证词不矛盾。

教学目标：证人可以因关系到其诚信的特定行为事例而被弹劾。证人也可以被那些反驳其关于案件中重要问题的证词的证据所弹劾。

References

Fed. R. Evid. 608(b) (impeaching witness's character for truthfulness with specific instances of conduct).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Impeachment (证据法：弹劾)
⚖️ 核心规则：FRE 608(b)

在交叉询问(Cross-Examination)中，允许询问证人关于其特定行为事例(Specific Instances of Conduct)，但必须满足以下条件：

  1. 该行为必须与诚信/真实性(Truthfulness/Veracity)有关；
  2. 目的是为了攻击证人的可信度；
  3. 不得引入外在证据(Extrinsic Evidence)来证明该行为。
🔍 案情分析

被告律师试图询问原告过去两次闯停车标志(Failing to stop)的经历。我们需要进行两步测试：

1. 诚信测试 (Veracity Test)
闯停车标志属于疏忽(Negligence)或违反交通规则，并不涉及欺诈、伪证或撒谎。因此，它不能反映原告是否是一个诚实的人。
结论 不符合 FRE 608(b)。

2. 矛盾测试 (Contradiction Test)
证人可以通过具体矛盾(Specific Contradiction)被弹劾。

  • 原告证词："我当时(at the time)开得很小心。"
  • 如果原告说："我从来没有违反过交通规则"，那么过去的罚单就可以用来反驳他。
  • 但原告只说了本次事故的情况。过去的疏忽并不反驳他在本次事故中小心驾驶的主张。

✅ 正确答案：选项 A

法院不应允许该提问。因为在其他场合未能停车：

  1. 与原告的真实性(Veracity)无关（不是撒谎行为）；
  2. 与本案证词不矛盾(Does not contradict)。
🚫 避坑指南
选项 B (Convictions)

错误逻辑：虽然 FRE 609 允许用刑事定罪(Conviction)弹劾，但 FRE 608(b) 允许询问未定罪的不良行为(Bad Acts)。选项B错误地暗示必须有定罪才能问。真正的拒绝理由是该行为与“诚实”无关。

选项 C (Credibility)

概念混淆：并非所有不良行为都影响可信度(Credibility)。只有涉及不诚实(Dishonesty)的行为才与作为证人的可信度相关。

选项 D (Contradiction)

范围错误：这是一种“性格证据”(Character Evidence)的伪装。不能用“他过去粗心”来证明“他这次也粗心”（除非符合 FRE 404(b) 的例外，本案不符）。这不构成法律上的“反驳”(Contradiction)。

💡 MBE 考试技巧

当看到律师想问证人过去的“坏事”时，请立即检查：

  1. 是撒谎吗？ (欺诈、伪造、作伪证) → 如果是，可以问 (FRE 608)。
  2. 是暴力或疏忽吗？ (打人、超速、闯红灯) → 通常不能问，除非证人自己把门打开了（例如声称自己是和平主义者或完美司机）。

questions.question:
A plaintiff sued a nonprofit organization after falling down a small set of stairs while visiting its headquarters. The plaintiff alleges that the nonprofit was negligent in failing to adequately mark the stairs. The nonprofit argues that the stairs were adequately marked and that the plaintiff's failure to watch her step caused the fall. At trial, the nonprofit called a witness who testified that he saw the plaintiff looking down at her cellphone just before falling. On cross-examination, the plaintiff's attorney asked the witness whether he had ever made monetary donations to the nonprofit. The witness denied making any donations. The plaintiff's attorney now seeks to introduce donation records from the nonprofit that the witness had made 10 donations to the nonprofit over the past 5 years.
Are the donation records admissible?

choices.a: No, because the donation records are extrinsic evidence of the witness's conduct.
choices.b: No, because the donation records are hearsay not within an exception.
choices.c: Yes, as impeachment evidence of the witness's bias.
choices.d: Yes, as impeachment evidence of the witness's character for truthfulness.

data.questionStem:
Q87118

A plaintiff sued a nonprofit organization after falling down a small set of stairs while visiting its headquarters. The plaintiff alleges that the nonprofit was negligent in failing to adequately mark the stairs. The nonprofit argues that the stairs were adequately marked and that the plaintiff's failure to watch her step caused the fall. At trial, the nonprofit called a witness who testified that he saw the plaintiff looking down at her cellphone just before falling. On cross-examination, the plaintiff's attorney asked the witness whether he had ever made monetary donations to the nonprofit. The witness denied making any donations. The plaintiff's attorney now seeks to introduce donation records from the nonprofit that the witness had made 10 donations to the nonprofit over the past 5 years.

Are the donation records admissible?

一名原告在访问一个非营利组织总部时，从一小段楼梯上摔下后，对该组织提起了诉讼。原告声称，该非营利组织因未能充分标示楼梯而存在过失。该非营利组织辩称，楼梯有充分的标示，是原告自己没注意脚下才导致摔倒。在庭审中，该非营利组织传唤了一名证人，该证人作证称，他看到原告在摔倒前正低头看手机。在交叉询问中，原告的律师询问该证人是否曾向该非营利组织进行过金钱捐赠。该证人否认进行过任何捐赠。原告的律师现在试图引入该非营利组织的捐赠记录，记录显示该证人在过去5年中向该非营利组织进行了10次捐赠。

这些捐赠记录是否可以采纳？
options:
A. No, because the donation records are extrinsic evidence of the witness's conduct.
不可以，因为捐赠记录是关于证人行为的外部证据。

B. No, because the donation records are hearsay not within an exception.
不可以，因为捐赠记录是传闻证据，且不属于例外情况。

C. Yes, as impeachment evidence of the witness's bias.
可以，作为弹劾证人偏见的证据。

D. Yes, as impeachment evidence of the witness's character for truthfulness.
可以，作为弹劾证人诚信品格的证据。
data.explanation:
A party may attack the credibility of a witness's testimony by introducing evidence that the witness is biased and therefore had a motive to lie while testifying. This can be done by introducing a specific instance of conduct (SIC) that illustrates the witness's bias through:
  • intrinsic evidence - by questioning the witness about the conduct or
  • extrinsic evidence - from any source other than the witness's own testimony.
Here, the plaintiff cross-examined the witness about his monetary donations to show his bias in favor of the nonprofit (intrinsic evidence). The witness denied the donations, so the plaintiff now seeks to introduce donation records from the nonprofit (extrinsic evidence). Since extrinsic evidence can also be used to show a witness's bias, the donation records are admissible.

(Choice A) Extrinsic evidence of a SIC is admissible to impeach a witness unless the SIC is a bad act that is probative of the witness's character for truthfulness (not seen here). In that case, only intrinsic evidence of the bad act is admissible and, if the witness denies the bad act, the examining party is stuck with that answer and cannot rebut it.

(Choice B) Hearsay refers to out-of-court statements (eg, donation records) offered for the truth of the matter asserted therein (eg, that donations were made). Such statements are inadmissible unless they are excluded or excepted from the rule against hearsay. And here, the nonprofit's donation records would likely fall within the exception for business records.

(Choice D) Although the donation records are being used to impeach the witness's testimony, they are not being used to attack the witness's character for truthfulness. That is because donations to the nonprofit do not suggest that the witness has a general propensity for dishonesty.

Educational objective: The credibility of a witness's testimony can be attacked with evidence (eg, a specific instance of conduct) that shows the witness's bias introduced (1) intrinsically through the witness's own testimony or (2) extrinsically through any other source.



选项正确率统计：A选项 35%，B选项 1%，C选项 46%（正确选项），D选项 15%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

一方当事人可以通过引入证据来攻击一名证人证词的可信度，该证据表明证人存在偏见，因此在作证时有说谎的动机。这可以通过引入能说明证人偏见的特定行为事例 (SIC) 来实现，其方式包括：
  • 内部证据 - 通过就该行为询问证人或
  • 外部证据 - 来自证人本人证词以外的任何来源。
在本案中，原告就证人的金钱捐赠对其进行交叉询问，以显示其对该非营利组织的偏见（内部证据）。该证人否认了这些捐赠，因此原告现在试图引入该非营利组织的捐赠记录（外部证据）。由于外部证据也可以用来显示证人的偏见，因此这些捐赠记录是可采纳的。

(选项A) 用于弹劾证人的特定行为事例的外部证据是可采纳的，除非该特定行为事例是能证明证人诚信品格的不良行为（本案情况并非如此）。在这种情况下，只有关于该不良行为的内部证据才可采纳，并且，如果证人否认该不良行为，询问方必须接受该回答，不得反驳。

(选项B) 传闻证据指的是庭外陈述（例如，捐赠记录），被用以证明其所主张事项的真实性（例如，证明捐赠确实发生）。此类陈述不可采纳，除非它们被排除在传闻证据规则之外或属于其例外情况。而在本案中，该非营利组织的捐赠记录很可能属于业务记录的例外情况。

(选项D) 尽管捐赠记录被用于弹劾证人的证词，但它们并非用于攻击证人的诚信品格。这是因为向非营利组织捐款并不表明该证人有普遍的不诚实倾向。

教学目标：证人证词的可信度可以通过显示其偏见的证据（例如，特定行为事例）来攻击，该证据可以通过（1）证人自身的证词（内部证据）或（2）任何其他来源（外部证据）的方式引入。

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

证据法：证人弹劾 (Impeachment)
正确答案 C. 可以，作为弹劾证人偏见的证据。
(Yes, as impeachment evidence of the witness's bias.)
核心考点：偏见 (Bias)

本题的核心在于区分偏见 (Bias) 与诚实品格 (Character for Truthfulness) 在引入外部证据 (Extrinsic Evidence) 时的规则差异。

法律规则：

为了证明证人存在偏见（例如：对一方当事人的敌意、偏爱、经济利益关系等），外部证据总是可采纳的 (Extrinsic evidence is admissible)。

虽然联邦证据规则 (FRE) 没有明确列出这一条，但根据最高法院判例 (United States v. Abel)，证明偏见不仅相关，而且不受“附带问题规则” (Collateral Evidence Rule) 的限制。

案情分析

在本案中：

  • 目的：原告律师试图证明证人偏袒非营利组织（被告）。
  • 手段：询问证人是否捐过款。
  • 冲突：证人否认捐款。
  • 对策：律师拿出捐款记录（外部证据）来反驳。

因为捐款显示了证人对被告的支持和潜在的利益关系，这属于偏见 (Bias)。因此，即使证人否认，律师也可以引入外部证据（捐款记录）来证明这一点。

易错点辨析：选项 A 的陷阱

很多考生会误选 A，混淆了 FRE 608(b) 规则。

比较项目 偏见 (Bias) 特定不诚实行为 (Specific Bad Acts - FRE 608(b))
定义 证人有动机撒谎（如亲属、金钱关系）。 证人过去撒过谎（如欺诈、伪造），证明其人品不可信。
外部证据 ✔ 允许 (Admissible) ✖ 禁止 (Inadmissible)
如果证人否认 可以用文件/其他证人反驳。 必须接受证人的回答 (Stuck with the answer)。

选项 A 错误的原因在于，它引用了 FRE 608(b) 的规则（禁止外部证据证明特定行为），但该规则仅适用于攻击“诚实品格”。本题攻击的是“偏见”，不受此限。

关于传闻证据 (Hearsay)

选项 B 错误。虽然捐赠记录是庭外陈述，但它们几乎肯定符合业务记录例外 (Business Records Exception, FRE 803(6))。题目问的是“是否可采纳”，既然符合传闻例外且用于证明偏见，它就是可采纳的。

💡 MBE 解题技巧
看到“外部证据” (Extrinsic Evidence) 被用来弹劾证人时，先问自己：这是为了证明什么？
  • 如果是证明偏见 (Bias) ➡ 允许。
  • 如果是证明感官缺陷 (Sensory Defect) ➡ 允许。
  • 如果是证明以前的不一致陈述 (Prior Inconsistent Statement) ➡ 有条件允许 (需给证人解释机会)。
  • 如果是证明过去的不良行为 (Bad Acts/Truthfulness) ➡ 禁止 (只能问，不能以此引入文件)。
本题中，“捐款” = “喜欢被告” = “偏见”，所以绿灯通行！

questions.question:
In contract litigation between a plaintiff and a defendant, a fact of consequence to the determination of the action is whether the plaintiff provided the defendant with a required notice at the defendant's branch office "in the state capital." The plaintiff introduced evidence that he gave notice at the defendant's office in City X. Although City X is the state's capital, the plaintiff failed to offer proof of that fact.
Which of the following statements is most clearly correct with respect to possible judicial notice of the fact that City X is the state's capital?

choices.a: If the court takes judicial notice, it should instruct the jury that it may, but is not required to, accept as conclusive the fact that City X is the capital.
choices.b: If the court takes judicial notice, the burden of persuasion on the issue of whether City X is the capital shifts to the defendant.
choices.c: The court may take judicial notice even though the plaintiff does not request it.
choices.d: The court may take judicial notice only if the plaintiff provides the court with an authenticated copy of the statute that designates City X as the capital.

data.questionStem:
Q87076

In contract litigation between a plaintiff and a defendant, a fact of consequence to the determination of the action is whether the plaintiff provided the defendant with a required notice at the defendant's branch office "in the state capital." The plaintiff introduced evidence that he gave notice at the defendant's office in City X. Although City X is the state's capital, the plaintiff failed to offer proof of that fact.

Which of the following statements is most clearly correct with respect to possible judicial notice of the fact that City X is the state's capital?

在原告与被告之间的一场合同诉讼中，一个对案件裁决具有关键影响的事实是，原告是否在被告位于“州首府”的分支机构向被告提供了法定的通知。原告提出的证据表明，他在被告位于X市的办公室发出了通知。尽管X市是该州的首府，但原告未能就此事实提供证明。

关于法院可能对X市是州首府这一事实进行司法认知，以下哪项陈述最为明确正确？
options:
A. If the court takes judicial notice, it should instruct the jury that it may, but is not required to, accept as conclusive the fact that City X is the capital.
如果法院采用司法认知，则应指示陪审团，其可以但非必须接受X市是州首府这一事实为定论。

B. If the court takes judicial notice, the burden of persuasion on the issue of whether City X is the capital shifts to the defendant.
如果法院采用司法认知，关于X市是否是州首府这一问题的说服责任将转移至被告。

C. The court may take judicial notice even though the plaintiff does not request it.
即使原告未提出请求，法院也可以采用司法认知。

D. The court may take judicial notice only if the plaintiff provides the court with an authenticated copy of the statute that designates City X as the capital.
法院仅在原告向其提供了指定X市为州首府的经认证的法规副本时，才可以采用司法认知。
data.explanation:
Judicial notice of adjudicative facts


(FRE 201) Case typeTaking noticeInstructing jury
CivilCourt:
  • may take notice on its own
  • must take notice if party requests & supplies necessary information
Jury must accept noticed fact as conclusive
CriminalJury may accept noticed fact as conclusive

FRE = Federal Rule of Evidence

Judicial notice is the court's acceptance of a fact as true without the need for a party to prove that fact. Under Federal Rule of Evidence 201, the court may take judicial notice of any adjudicative fact that is not subject to reasonable dispute - eg, the fact that City X is the state's capital. The court:

  • may take judicial notice sua sponte (ie, on its own initiative)
  • must take judicial notice if a party requests it and supplies the court with the necessary information to indicate that the fact is not subject to reasonable dispute (Choice D).

Therefore, the court may take judicial notice of the fact that City X is the state's capital even though the plaintiff does not request it. And since this contract litigation is a civil case, that judicial notice is binding on the jury. This means that the jury should be instructed that it must accept the noticed fact as conclusive (Choice A).

The court may not take judicial notice of a fact based solely on the judge's own personal knowledge. Instead, the fact must be generally known within the community (ie, notorious) OR capable of being accurately and readily determined (ie, manifest).

(Choice B) Once judicial notice is taken in this civil case, the issue of whether City X is the capital is decided and the jury cannot weigh the evidence or reach its own conclusion on this issue. As a result, there is no burden of persuasion (ie, standard of proof) on this issue.

Educational objective: A court can take judicial notice of an adjudicative fact that is not subject to reasonable dispute (1) on its own initiative or (2) at a party's request.

And in a civil case, a noticed fact is binding on the jury.



选项正确率统计：A选项 15%，B选项 4%，C选项 78%（正确选项），D选项 2%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

对裁决事实的司法认知


(FRE 201) 案件类型采用认知指示陪审团
民事案件法院：
  • 可以依职权主动采用认知
  • 如果一方当事人请求并提供必要信息，则必须采用认知
陪审团必须接受经认知的事实为定论
刑事案件陪审团可以接受经认知的事实为定论

FRE = Federal Rule of Evidence

司法认知是法院接受某一事实为真实，而无需一方当事人证明该事实。根据《Federal Rule of Evidence 201》，法院可以对任何不存在合理争议的裁决事实进行司法认知——例如，X市是州首府这一事实。法院：

  • 可以依职权（即主动）进行司法认知
  • 如果一方当事人提出请求，并向法院提供必要信息以表明该事实不存在合理争议，则法院必须进行司法认知（选项D）。

因此，即使原告未提出请求，法院也可以对X市是州首府这一事实进行司法认知。并且，由于此合同诉讼是民事案件，该司法认知对陪审团具有约束力。这意味着应指示陪审团，其必须接受该经认知的事实为定论（选项A）。

法院不得仅根据法官本人的个人知识对某一事实进行司法认知。相反，该事实必须是社区内普遍知晓的（即众所周知的），或者能够被准确、便捷地确定（即显而易见的）。

（选项B）在此民事案件中，一旦进行了司法认知，X市是否是州首府的问题即已确定，陪审团不能对此问题衡量证据或得出自己的结论。因此，此问题不存在说服责任（即证明标准）。

教学目的：法院可以对不存在合理争议的裁决事实进行司法认知，其方式可以是（1）依职权主动进行，或（2）应一方当事人的请求进行。

并且，在民事案件中，经认知的事实对陪审团具有约束力。



References

Fed. R. Evid. 201 (judicial notice).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence Law (证据法)
核心考点：司法认知 (Judicial Notice)

本题考察 FRE 201 关于裁决事实 (Adjudicative Facts) 的司法认知规则。

司法认知是指法院在无需当事人举证的情况下，直接确认某一事实为真。

为什么选 C？(Correct Answer)

规则依据：根据《联邦证据规则》第 201(c) 条，法院对司法认知拥有自由裁量权 (Discretionary Power)。

  • Sua Sponte (依职权)： 法院可以在没有当事人请求的情况下，主动对事实进行司法认知。
  • Mandatory (强制性)： 只有当一方当事人提出请求并提供了必要信息时，法院才必须进行司法认知。

本案应用： "X市是州首府" 是一个地理/政治常识，属于无合理争议 (Not subject to reasonable dispute) 的事实。虽然原告没有请求，法官完全有权主动（May）进行认知。

关键陷阱：民事 vs 刑事

MBE 最喜欢考察司法认知在不同案件类型中对陪审团的效力区别（排除选项 A 的关键）。

案件类型 陪审团指示 (Jury Instruction)
民事案件 (Civil)
本题情况		 陪审团 必须 (Must) 接受该事实为定论 (Conclusive)。
刑事案件 (Criminal) 陪审团 可以 (May) 接受该事实，但非必须。
选项 A 错误 混淆了规则： 选项 A 描述的是刑事案件的规则。本题是合同纠纷（民事），司法认知对陪审团具有强制约束力。
选项 B 错误 举证责任： 司法认知一旦做出，该事实即被确立，不再需要举证或说服。它不是转移举证责任，而是免除了举证责任。
选项 D 错误 条件过严： 法院可以主动认知，不需要原告提供认证副本。只有在要求法院必须认知时，才需要提供充分信息。
💡 MBE 备考锦囊 遇到 Judicial Notice 的题目，按以下步骤思考：
  1. 看事实： 是否属于常识或易于验证（如地理位置、日历日期）？
  2. 看类型： 是 Civil 还是 Criminal？
    • Civil -> Must accept.
    • Criminal -> May accept.
  3. 看请求： 有请求+资料=必须认知；无请求=法官可以认知。

questions.question:
A plaintiff sued an individual defendant for injuries suffered in a collision between the plaintiff's car and the defendant's truck while the defendant's employee was driving the truck. The plaintiff sought discovery of any accident report the employee might have made to the defendant, but the defendant responded that no such report existed. Before trial, the defendant moved to preclude the plaintiff from asking the defendant in the presence of the jury whether he had destroyed such a report because the defendant would then invoke his privilege against self-incrimination.
Should the court allow the plaintiff to ask the defendant about the destruction of the report?

choices.a: No, because a report that was prepared in anticipation of litigation is not subject to discovery.
choices.b: No, because no inference may properly be drawn from invocation of a legitimate privilege.
choices.c: Yes, because a party in a civil action may not invoke the privilege against self-incrimination.
choices.d: Yes, because the defendant's destruction of the report could serve as the basis of an inference adverse to the defendant.

Q87095

A plaintiff sued an individual defendant for injuries suffered in a collision between the plaintiff's car and the defendant's truck while the defendant's employee was driving the truck. The plaintiff sought discovery of any accident report the employee might have made to the defendant, but the defendant responded that no such report existed. Before trial, the defendant moved to preclude the plaintiff from asking the defendant in the presence of the jury whether he had destroyed such a report because the defendant would then invoke his privilege against self-incrimination.

Should the court allow the plaintiff to ask the defendant about the destruction of the report?

一名原告因其汽车与被告雇员驾驶的卡车发生碰撞而受伤，因此起诉了该个人被告。原告请求证据开示，要求被告提供其雇员可能已向被告提交的任何事故报告，但被告回应称不存在此类报告。在庭审前，被告提出动议，请求预先禁止原告在陪审团在场的情况下，询问被告是否销毁了该报告，因为被告届时会援引其反对自证其罪的特权。

法院是否应允许原告就被告销毁报告一事进行询问？
options:
A. No, because a report that was prepared in anticipation of litigation is not subject to discovery.
不应，因为为预期诉讼而准备的报告不受证据开示的约束。

B. No, because no inference may properly be drawn from invocation of a legitimate privilege.
不应，因为从援引一项合法特权的行为中，不得做出任何恰当的推断。

C. Yes, because a party in a civil action may not invoke the privilege against self-incrimination.
应该，因为在民事诉讼中，当事人不得援引反对自证其罪的特权。

D. Yes, because the defendant's destruction of the report could serve as the basis of an inference adverse to the defendant.
应该，因为被告销毁报告的行为可作为对被告作出不利推断的基础。
data.explanation:
Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination


Allows any witness (including party-witnesses) in civil & criminal proceedings to refuse to give potentially incriminating testimony
In civil case, opposing party may ask jury to draw adverse inference from witness's claim of privilege
In criminal case, prosecution cannot comment on defendant's failure to take stand & cannot ask jury to draw adverse inference from defendant's claim of privilege
A party can generally present evidence to support an adverse inference against the opposing party. For example, the intentional destruction of relevant evidence can create an adverse inference that such evidence would have been unfavorable to the party that destroyed it. And in civil cases, an adverse inference can also be drawn from a party's invocation of the Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. Therefore, the court should allow the plaintiff to ask the defendant about the destruction of the accident report to raise these inferences.

(Choice A) The accident report would qualify as work product if it was prepared by or for an attorney in anticipation of litigation - but that cannot be determined based on the facts provided. Even if it is work product, this privilege would only protect the report from discovery - not prevent the plaintiff from asking if the report had been destroyed.

(Choice B) Had this been a criminal case, the prosecutor would have been prohibited from commenting on the defendant's invocation of the privilege against self-incrimination. The jury would also have been barred from drawing a negative inference from the assertion of that privilege.

(Choice C) The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination applies in civil and criminal cases.

Educational objective: A party can generally present evidence to support an adverse inference against the opposing party, including evidence on the intentional destruction of relevant evidence. And in civil cases only, a party can ask the jury to draw an adverse inference from the opposing party's invocation of the privilege against self-incrimination.

选项正确率统计：A选项 6%，B选项 13%，C选项 13%，D选项 66%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

《第五修正案》反对自证其罪的特权


允许民事和刑事诉讼中的任何证人（包括当事人作为证人时）拒绝提供可能构成自证其罪的证词
在民事案件中，对方当事人可以请求陪审团从证人主张特权的行为中作出不利推断
在刑事案件中，控方不得就被告不行使作证权利一事发表评论，也不得请求陪审团从被告主张特权的行为中作出不利推断
一方当事人通常可以提出证据，以支持对对方当事人作出不利推断。例如，故意销毁相关证据的行为，可以产生一种不利推断，即该证据本会对销毁方不利。并且，在民事案件中，也可以从一方当事人援引《第五修正案》反对自证其罪的特权的行为中作出不利推断。因此，法院应允许原告就被告销毁事故报告一事进行询问，以引出这些推断。

(选项A) 如果事故报告是由律师或为律师准备以预期诉讼，则该报告将符合“律师工作成果”的资格——但这无法根据所提供的事实来确定。即使它是律师工作成果，这项特权也只能保护报告免于证据开示——而不能阻止原告询问该报告是否已被销毁。

(选项B) 如果这是一个刑事案件，检察官将被禁止就被告援引反对自证其罪的特权发表评论。陪审团也将被禁止从该特权的主张中作出不利推断。

(选项C) 《第五修正案》反对自证其罪的特权适用于民事和刑事案件。

教学目标：一方当事人通常可以提出证据以支持对对方当事人作出不利推断，包括关于故意销毁相关证据的证据。并且，仅在民事案件中，一方当事人可以请求陪审团从对方当事人援引反对自证其罪的特权的行为中作出不利推断。

MBE 考点解析：证据法

Topic: Fifth Amendment in Civil Cases

正确答案：D

法院应该允许原告询问。因为被告销毁报告的行为可以作为对被告作出不利推断 (Adverse Inference) 的基础。

核心考点：民事案件中的第五修正案

本题考察的是《第五修正案》反对自证其罪特权 (Privilege Against Self-Incrimination) 在民事诉讼中的适用规则。

虽然第五修正案适用于民事和刑事案件，但其后果截然不同：

案件类型 能否援引特权？ 能否作出不利推断？
刑事案件
Criminal		 可以 不可以
检方不能评论，陪审团不能推断。
民事案件
Civil		 可以 可以
陪审团可以根据当事人的沉默作出对其不利的推断。

判例依据： Baxter v. Palmigiano (1976)。最高法院裁定，在民事诉讼中，如果一方当事人援引第五修正案拒绝回答问题，法院允许事实认定者（陪审团）由此作出不利推断。

本题逻辑推演
  1. 销毁证据 (Spoliation of Evidence)： 故意销毁相关证据本身就允许陪审团推断该证据对销毁方不利。
  2. 特权的使用： 被告试图通过援引第五修正案来阻止原告在陪审团面前提问。
  3. 结论： 由于这是民事案件，原告有权询问。如果被告选择援引特权拒绝回答，陪审团有权得知这一情况，并推断被告是因为“心虚”或报告内容对其不利才销毁了报告。
干扰项辨析
选项 A 错误 (Work Product)
即使报告属于“律师工作成果”，该特权仅保护文件不被开示 (Discovery)。它并不禁止询问关于“是否销毁了文件”这一事实。此外，销毁证据本身可能构成犯罪或制裁理由，特权不能用来掩盖销毁行为。
选项 B 错误 (No Inference)
这是刑事案件的规则。在民事案件中，援引特权是可以导致不利推断的。
选项 C 错误 (No Privilege in Civil)
表述错误。当事人在民事案件中确实拥有第五修正案特权（如果回答可能导致刑事责任），只是行使该特权会有不利的民事后果（即不利推断）。
💡 MBE 考试技巧：
看到“第五修正案”时，第一反应要区分是Civil还是Criminal。
如果是Civil Case，记住：Silence is expensive.（沉默是有代价的）。当事人可以不说话，但陪审团可以假设他隐瞒了坏事。

questions.question:
At the defendant's trial for burglary, a witness supported the defendant's alibi that they were fishing together at the time of the crime. On cross-examination, the witness was asked whether his statement on a credit card application that he had worked for his present employer for the last five years was false. The witness denied that the statement was false.
The prosecutor then calls the manager of the company for which the witness works to testify that although the witness had been first employed five years earlier and is now employed by the company, there had been a three-year period during which he had not been so employed.
Is the manager's testimony admissible or inadmissible?

choices.a: Admissible, as a matter of right, because the witness "opened the door" by his denial on cross-examination.
choices.b: Admissible, in the judge's discretion, because the witness's credibility is a fact of major consequence to the case.
choices.c: Inadmissible, because the misstatement by the witness could have been caused by misunderstanding of the application form.
choices.d: Inadmissible, because whether the witness lied in his application is a matter that cannot be proved by extrinsic evidence.

data.questionStem:
Q87088

At the defendant's trial for burglary, a witness supported the defendant's alibi that they were fishing together at the time of the crime. On cross- examination, the witness was asked whether his statement on a credit card application that he had worked for his present employer for the last five years was false. The witness denied that the statement was false.

The prosecutor then calls the manager of the company for which the witness works to testify that although the witness had been first employed five years earlier and is now employed by the company, there had been a three-year period during which he had not been so employed.

Is the manager's testimony admissible or inadmissible?

在被告的入室犯法罪审判中，一名证人支持了被告的不在场证明，称案发时他们正在一起钓鱼。在交叉询问中，该证人被问及，其在信用卡申请表上所作的“过去五年一直在为现任雇主工作”的陈述是否虚假。证人否认该陈述为虚假。

随后，检察官传唤该证人所工作的公司的经理作证，称该证人虽然在五年前首次受雇于该公司且目前仍在该公司任职，但期间曾有三年时间并未受雇。

该经理的证言是可采纳的还是不可采纳的？
options:
A. Admissible, as a matter of right, because the witness "opened the door" by his denial on cross-examination.
可采纳，作为一项权利，因为证人在交叉询问中的否认“打开了方便之门”。

B. Admissible, in the judge's discretion, because the witness's credibility is a fact of major consequence to the case.
可采纳，由法官酌情决定，因为证人的可信度是对案件具有重大影响的事实。

C. Inadmissible, because the misstatement by the witness could have been caused by misunderstanding of the application form.
不可采纳，因为证人的不实陈述可能是由于对申请表的误解所致。

D. Inadmissible, because whether the witness lied in his application is a matter that cannot be proved by extrinsic evidence.
不可采纳，因为证人是否在申请中撒谎是一个不能通过外部证据证明的事项。
data.explanation:
Any party can impeach (ie, discredit) a witness's character for truthfulness by presenting either:
  • reputation or opinion testimony about the witness's untruthful character or
  • specific instances of conduct (SICs) that are indicative of the witness's untruthful character.


If the SIC involves a criminal conviction for a felony or crime of dishonesty, it can be introduced intrinsically (ie, through that witness's own testimony) or extrinsically (ie, from any other source). Otherwise, the SIC can only be introduced intrinsically. And if the witness denies the SIC (and it does not involve a qualifying conviction), that denial cannot be rebutted by extrinsic evidence.

Here, the prosecutor attacked the alibi witness's character for truthfulness on cross-examination by asking him about a SIC involving a false statement on a credit card application. Although the witness denied that the statement was false, the prosecutor cannot use extrinsic evidence (eg, the manager's testimony) to rebut that denial since the SIC does not involve a qualifying criminal conviction (Choice A). Therefore, the manager's testimony is inadmissible.

(Choice B) Extrinsic evidence can always be used to prove a fact of major consequence - ie, one that is material to the case. But a witness's credibility is merely a collateral (ie, immaterial) matter, so it can only be attacked with extrinsic evidence of a SIC involving a qualifying criminal conviction (not seen here).

(Choice C) The reason for the witness's misstatement does not factor into whether the manager's impeachment testimony is admissible.

Educational objective: Intrinsic evidence of a specific instance of conduct (SIC) can always be used to impeach a witness's character for truthfulness. But extrinsic evidence can only be used if the SIC involves conviction for a felony or crime of dishonesty.



选项正确率统计：A选项 10%，B选项 16%，C选项 3%，D选项 70%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

任何一方均可弹劾（即，质疑其可信度）一名证人关于其诚实性的品格，通过出示以下任一证据：
  • 关于该证人不诚实品格的名誉或意见证词，或者
  • 能表明该证人不诚实品格的特定行为事例 (SICs)。


如果特定行为事例涉及重罪或不诚实罪的刑事定罪，则可以通过内在方式（即通过该证人自己的证词）或外在方式（即从任何其他来源）引入。否则，该特定行为事例只能通过内在方式引入。并且，如果证人否认该特定行为事例（且该事例不涉及符合条件的定罪），该否认不能通过外在证据来反驳。

在本案中，检察官在交叉询问中，通过询问不在场证明证人关于信用卡申请表上虚假陈述的特定行为事例，来攻击其诚实品格。尽管证人否认该陈述为虚假，但由于该特定行为事例不涉及符合条件的刑事定罪，检察官不能使用外在证据（例如，经理的证词）来反驳该否认(选项 A)。因此，该经理的证词是不可采纳的。

(选项 B) 外在证据总是可以用来证明具有重大影响的事实——即对案件有实质性关系的事实。但证人的可信度仅仅是一个附带（即非实质性）事项，因此只能通过涉及符合条件的刑事定罪的特定行为事例的外在证据（本案中未出现）来攻击。

(选项 C) 证人作出不实陈述的原因，并非决定该经理的弹劾证词是否可采纳的因素。

教学目标： 关于特定行为事例 (SIC) 的内在证据总是可以用来弹劾证人的诚实品格。但是，只有当该特定行为事例涉及重罪或不诚实罪的定罪时，才能使用外在证据。

References

  • Fed. R. Evid. 607 (who may impeach witness).
  • Fed. R. Evid. 608 (witness's character for truthfulness).
  • Fed. R. Evid. 404 (character evidence; crimes or other acts).
  • Fed. R. Evid. 405 (methods of proving character).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析：证据法

本题考察的是联邦证据规则（Federal Rules of Evidence, FRE）中关于弹劾证人（Impeachment）的核心规则，特别是关于使用“特定行为事例”来攻击证人诚实性的限制。

正确答案：D
⚖️ 核心法律规则：FRE 608(b)

在交叉询问（Cross-examination）中，允许询问证人关于其过去表明其不诚实的特定行为事例（Specific Instances of Conduct）。

但是（关键限制）：如果证人否认该行为，提问方不得使用外部证据（Extrinsic Evidence）来证明该行为确实发生过。

逻辑推演步骤

1. 识别证据类型
检察官询问证人在信用卡申请表上撒谎（虚报工作年限）。这是一个并未导致刑事定罪（Conviction）的不良行为，但它与证人的诚实性（Character for Truthfulness）直接相关。
2. 交叉询问阶段（允许）
根据 FRE 608(b)，检察官有权在交叉询问时问这个问题：“你在申请表上撒谎了吗？”这是为了攻击证人的可信度。
3. 证人的回答
证人否认了这一指控（"The witness denied that the statement was false"）。
4. 外部证据规则（禁止）
当证人否认后，检察官试图传唤公司经理作证。经理的证词属于外部证据（Extrinsic Evidence）。

法律规定，对于仅仅用来攻击证人诚实性的“特定行为事例”（非刑事定罪），提问方必须“接受证人的回答”（Stuck with the answer）。你不能为了证明证人在刚才的小问题上撒谎，而开启一个“案中案”（Mini-trial）。

为什么选 D？

选项 D 准确地陈述了 FRE 608(b) 的规则：证人是否在申请表上撒谎是一个附带事项（Collateral Matter），不能通过外部证据（即经理的证词）来证明。一旦证人否认，检察官就不能再深究了。

为什么其他选项是错的？

  • 选项 A (Opened the door): 错误。证人的单纯否认并没有“打开大门”允许引入被禁止的外部证据。只有当证据涉及案件的核心事实（Material Fact）而非仅仅是证人品格时，否认才允许反驳。
  • 选项 B (Major consequence): 错误。虽然证人的可信度很重要，但法律为了节约庭审时间，禁止在附带问题（如几年前是否在表格上撒谎）上纠缠。这被称为“附带证据规则”（Collateral Evidence Rule）。
  • 选项 C (Misunderstanding): 错误。这解释了证人可能没撒谎的原因，但这与证据是否可采纳（Admissible）的法律规则无关。
🎓 考场技巧 (Exam Tip)

遇到“特定坏行为”（Bad Acts）考题时，请记住口诀：
"You can ask, but you can't prove."
（你可以问，但不能用外部证据证明。）

*注意区分：如果是刑事定罪（Conviction, FRE 609），则通常可以引入法庭记录作为外部证据。

questions.question:
A plaintiff sued a defendant for damages arising out of an automobile collision. At trial, the plaintiff called an eyewitness to the collision. The plaintiff expected the eyewitness to testify that she had observed the defendant's automobile for five seconds prior to the collision and estimated the defendant's speed at the time of the collision to have been 50 miles per hour. Instead, the eyewitness testified that she estimated the defendant's speed to have been 25 miles per hour. When asked whether she had ever claimed to have seen the defendant going faster than 25 miles per hour, the eyewitness denied making such a statement.
Without finally excusing the eyewitness, the plaintiff then called a second witness, a police officer, to testify that the eyewitness had told him during his investigation at the accident scene that the defendant "was doing at least 50."
Is the police officer's testimony admissible?

choices.a: No, because it is hearsay not within any exception.
choices.b: No, because the plaintiff may not impeach his own witness.
choices.c: Yes, as a present sense impression.
choices.d: Yes, in order to impeach the eyewitness.

questions.question:
A man suffered a broken jaw in a fight with a neighbor that took place when they were both spectators at a soccer match. The man sues the neighbor for personal-injury damages.
Which of the following actions must the trial court take if requested by the man?

choices.a: Exclude nonparty eyewitnesses from the courtroom during the testimony of other witnesses.
choices.b: Prevent the neighbor's principal eyewitness from testifying, upon a showing that six years ago the witness was convicted of perjury and the conviction has not been the subject of a pardon or annulment.
choices.c: Refuse to let the neighbor cross-examine the man's medical expert on matters not covered on direct examination of the expert.
choices.d: Require the production of a writing used before trial to refresh a witness's memory.

data.questionStem: Q87115 A man suffered a broken jaw in a fight with a neighbor that took place when they were both spectators at a soccer match. The man sues the neighbor for personal-injury damages. Which of the following actions must the trial court take if requested by the man? 一名男子在与邻居的一场争斗中下颚骨折，事发时两人正在观看一场足球比赛。该男子以人身伤害为由起诉其邻居，要求赔偿。 如果该男子提出请求，初审法院必须采取以下哪项行动？
options:
A. Exclude nonparty eyewitnesses from the courtroom during the testimony of other witnesses.
在其他证人作证期间，将非当事方的目击证人排除在法庭之外。

B. Prevent the neighbor's principal eyewitness from testifying, upon a showing that six years ago the witness was convicted of perjury and the conviction has not been the subject of a pardon or annulment.
在证明邻居的主要目击证人六年前曾因伪证罪被定罪，且该定罪未经赦免或撤销的情况下，阻止其作证。

C. Refuse to let the neighbor cross-examine the man's medical expert on matters not covered on direct examination of the expert.
拒绝让邻居就该男子医疗专家在直接询问中未涉及的事项对该专家进行交叉询问。

D. Require the production of a writing used before trial to refresh a witness's memory.
要求出示一份在审判前用于唤醒证人记忆的书面文件。
data.explanation:
Exclusion of witnesses


(FRE 615) Court must exclude witnesses upon party's request - and may do so on court's own initiative - unless:
  • witness is party or its designated representative
  • witness's presence is essential to party's presentation of its case
  • witness is authorized by statute to be present
FRE = Federal Rule of Evidence

Federal Rule of Evidence (FRE) 615 - often referred to as "the Rule" - provides that a court must , upon a party's request , exclude witnesses from the courtroom so they cannot hear other witnesses' testimony. A court may also sequester witnesses on its own initiative. However, the Rule cannot be used to exclude :
  • parties or their designated representatives
  • persons whose presence is shown to be essential to a party's presentation of its case (eg, expert witness) or
  • persons authorized by statute to be present (eg, crime victim)


Here, there is no indication that (1) a party has shown the nonparty eyewitnesses' presence to be essential to its case or (2) those witnesses are authorized by statute to be present. Therefore, the trial court must, at the man's request, remove the witnesses from the courtroom during the testimony of other witnesses.

(Choice B) A witness cannot be prevented from testifying simply because he/she has been convicted of a crime - even perjury. Instead, evidence of that conviction may be admitted to impeach the witness.

(Choice C) FRE 611 limits the scope of cross-examination to matters addressed on direct examination or impacting the witness's credibility. But a court has broad discretion to allow questions beyond that scope, so it cannot be required to prohibit a cross-examiner from asking questions unrelated to the direct examination.

(Choice D) Under FRE 612, the court may order a party to produce a writing that was used before trial to refresh a witness's memory but is not required to do so upon another party's request.

Educational objective: A court must exclude a witness from the courtroom upon a party's request - or may do so on the court's own initiative - unless the witness is (1) a party or its designated representative, (2) a person whose presence is essential to the case, or (3) a person authorized by statute to be present.

选项正确率统计：A选项 61%（正确选项），B选项 8%，C选项 17%，D选项 12%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

证人隔离


(FRE 615) 法院必须应一方当事人的请求将证人隔离——也可以自行决定这样做——除非：
  • 证人是当事人或其指定代表
  • 证人的在场对一方当事人陈述其案情至关重要
  • 法律授权该证人在场
FRE = 《联邦证据规则》

《联邦证据规则》(FRE) 615——通常被称为“该规则”——规定，法院必须应一方当事人的请求，将证人排除在法庭之外，以使他们听不到其他证人的证词。法院也可以自行决定隔离证人。然而，该规则不能用于排除：
  • 当事人或其指定代表
  • 经证明其在场对一方当事人陈述案情至关重要的人员（例如，专家证人）或
  • 法律授权在场的人员（例如，犯罪受害人）


在本案中，没有迹象表明（1）一方当事人已证明非当事方目击证人的在场对其案情至关重要，或（2）那些证人被法律授权在场。因此，初审法院必须应男子的请求，在其他证人作证期间，将这些证人带离法庭。

（选项B）不能仅仅因为证人曾被判有罪——即使是伪证罪——就阻止其作证。相反，该定罪的证据可以被采纳以弹劾该证人。

（选项C）FRE 611 将交叉询问的范围限制在直接询问中处理的事项或影响证人可信度的事项。但法院拥有广泛的自由裁量权，可以允许超出该范围的提问，因此不能要求其禁止交叉询问人提出与直接询问无关的问题。

（选项D）根据FRE 612，法院可以命令一方当事人出示在审判前用于唤醒证人记忆的书面文件，但并非必须应另一方当事人的请求这样做。

教学目标：法院必须应一方当事人的请求将证人排除在法庭之外——或可自行决定这样做——除非该证人是（1）当事人或其指定代表，（2）其在场对案件至关重要的人员，或（3）法律授权在场的人员。

References

Fed. R. Evid. 615 (excluding witnesses).

MBE 考点解析

Evidence Law | FRE 615

本题考察的是《联邦证据规则》（Federal Rules of Evidence, FRE）中关于证人隔离（Sequestration of Witnesses）的强制性规定。

核心考点：FRE 615 该规则规定：应一方当事人的请求（At a party's request），法院必须（Must）下令将证人排除在法庭之外，以防止他们听到其他证人的证词。
✅ 正确答案分析 (选项 A)

法律依据：根据 FRE 615，证人隔离通常是强制性的（Mandatory）权利，而非法院的自由裁量权（Discretion）。

逻辑推理：

  • 题目中，原告（Man）提出了请求。
  • 被请求排除的是“非当事方目击证人”（Nonparty eyewitnesses）。
  • FRE 615 虽然有例外情况（如下文所述），但普通的目击证人通常不属于例外。
  • 因此，法院没有选择权，必须批准该请求。

FRE 615 的三个例外（不能排除的人）：

  1. 当事人（A party who is a natural person）；
  2. 当事人是法人时的指定代表（Designated representative）；
  3. 被证明其在场对案件陈述至关重要的人（如专家证人 Expert Witness）。

本题中的目击证人不属于上述任何例外，故必须被隔离。

❌ 干扰项快速排除
B 错误原因：资格与弹劾 (Competency vs. Impeachment)
根据 FRE 601，每个人都有作证资格。伪证罪（Perjury）定罪记录可用于弹劾（Impeach）证人的可信度（FRE 609），但不能作为完全阻止其作证的理由。
C 错误原因：交叉询问范围 (Scope of Cross)
虽然 FRE 611(b) 一般将交叉询问限制在直接询问的范围内，但它同时也赋予了法院自由裁量权（Discretion），允许法院批准超出范围的提问。题目问的是法院“必须”做什么，法院并非“必须”拒绝，而是“可以”允许。
D 错误原因：唤醒记忆 (Refreshing Recollection)
这是一个经典的 MBE 陷阱：
  • 如果文件是在作证时（While testifying）使用，必须出示。
  • 如果文件是在作证前（Before testifying）使用（如本题），根据 FRE 612，法院拥有自由裁量权决定是否要求出示（if justice requires），并非强制性“必须”。
🎓 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在 MBE 证据法题目中，务必区分：

  • Must (Mandatory): 法院必须执行（如 FRE 615 的证人隔离请求）。
  • May (Discretionary): 法院可以自行决定（如 FRE 611 交叉询问范围、FRE 612 作证前文件的出示）。

看到题目问 "must" 时，排除所有涉及司法自由裁量权的选项。

MBE Evidence Review © 2025

questions.question:
A plaintiff sued the defendant for dissolution of their yearlong partnership. One issue concerned the amount of money the plaintiff had received in cash. It was customary for the defendant to give the plaintiff money from the cash register as the plaintiff needed it for personal expenses. The plaintiff testified that, as he received money, he jotted down the amounts in the partnership ledger. Although the defendant had access to the ledger, she made no changes in it.
The ledger was admitted into evidence. The defendant seeks to testify to her memory of much larger amounts she had given the plaintiff.
Is the defendant's testimony admissible or inadmissible?

choices.a: Admissible, because it is based on the defendant's firsthand knowledge.
choices.b: Admissible, because the ledger entries offered by a party-opponent opened the door.
choices.c: Inadmissible, because the defendant's failure to challenge the accuracy of the ledger constituted an adoptive admission.
choices.d: Inadmissible, because the ledger is the best evidence of the amounts the plaintiff received.

data.questionStem:
Q87098

A plaintiff sued the defendant for dissolution of their yearlong partnership. One issue concerned the amount of money the plaintiff had received in cash. It was customary for the defendant to give the plaintiff money from the cash register as the plaintiff needed it for personal expenses. The plaintiff testified that, as he received money, he jotted down the amounts in the partnership ledger. Although the defendant had access to the ledger, she made no changes in it.

The ledger was admitted into evidence. The defendant seeks to testify to her memory of much larger amounts she had given the plaintiff.

Is the defendant's testimony admissible or inadmissible?

一名原告起诉被告，要求解散他们为期一年的合伙关系。其中一个争议点是原告收到的现金数额。按照惯例，当原告需要个人开销时，被告会从收银机中给他钱。原告作证称，每当他收到钱时，他都会在合伙企业的分类账中记下数额。尽管被告可以查阅该账本，但她并未对其进行任何修改。

该账本已被采纳为证据。被告试图就她记忆中曾给予原告的、数额大得多的款项作证。

被告的证言是否可采纳？
options:
A. Admissible, because it is based on the defendant's firsthand knowledge.
可采纳，因为该证言基于被告的第一手认知。

B. Admissible, because the ledger entries offered by a party-opponent opened the door.
可采纳，因为对方当事人提供的账本分录为此打开了大门。

C. Inadmissible, because the defendant's failure to challenge the accuracy of the ledger constituted an adoptive admission.
不可采纳，因为被告未能对账本的准确性提出质疑，构成了采纳性承认 (adoptive admission)。

D. Inadmissible, because the ledger is the best evidence of the amounts the plaintiff received.
不可采纳，因为该账本是证明原告所收款项数额的最佳证据。
data.explanation:
Witness testimony


Fact testimonyOpinion testimony
Lay witnessPersonal knowledge of factual matterProhibited unless common-sense impression that:
  • is rationally based on witness's perception
  • helps clarify witness's testimony or fact issue and
  • is not based on scientific/technical/specialized knowledge
Expert witnessAdmissible from qualified expert who:
  • testifies based on sufficient facts or data acquired by reliable principles & methods
  • has reasonable degree of certainty in opinion and
  • helps trier of fact understand evidence or fact issue
Has knowledge, skill, experience, training, or education in substantive area.
A lay witness can generally testify to any relevant matter based on his/her personal knowledge. This includes both:
  • factual matters that the witness perceived firsthand - eg, "I saw a man holding a beer bottle and slurring his words" and
  • common-sense impressions that are rationally based on those perceptions - eg, "The man was drunk."

Here, the defendant seeks to testify that the plaintiff received much larger amounts of cash than those recorded in a ledger. And since this testimony is based on the defendant's firsthand knowledge - her memory of the cash amounts she gave - it is admissible.

(Choice B) The defendant's testimony is admissible - regardless of whether the ledger had been offered by the plaintiff (the party- opponent) - because that testimony is relevant and based on her personal knowledge.

(Choice C) An adoptive admission is a hearsay exception that allows the admission of another's statement that a party-opponent has adopted as his/her own. Therefore, the defendant's failure to challenge the accuracy of the ledger may constitute an adoptive admission if a reasonable person would have done so. But this rule does not preclude the defendant's testimony rebutting the ledger's contents.

(Choice D) The best evidence rule generally requires that an original writing, recording, or photograph (eg, the ledger) be admitted to prove its contents. But this rule does not affect the admissibility of the defendant's testimony to rebut the ledger's contents.

Educational objective: A lay witness can generally testify to any relevant matter based on the witness's personal knowledge or a common-sense impression that is rationally based on such knowledge.

选项正确率统计：A选项 77%（正确选项），B选项 4%，C选项 8%，D选项 10%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

证人证言


事实证言意见证言
非专业证人对事实性事项的亲身认知禁止，除非是基于常识的观感，且该观感：
  • 合理地基于证人的感知
  • 有助于澄清证人的证言或事实争议点 并且
  • 并非基于科学/技术/专业知识
专家证人由具备资格的专家提供的证言可被采纳，该专家：
  • 基于通过可靠原则和方法获取的充分事实或数据作证
  • 其意见具有合理的确定性 并且
  • 有助于事实审判者理解证据或事实争议点
在实体领域拥有知识、技能、经验、培训或教育。
一名非专业证人通常可以就任何基于其亲身认知的相关事项作证。这包括：
  • 证人亲身感知的事实性事项——例如，“我看到一个男人拿着啤酒瓶，说话含糊不清” 并且
  • 合理地基于这些感知而形成的常识性观感——例如，“那个男人喝醉了。”

在本案中，被告试图作证，证明原告收到的现金数额远大于账本上记录的数额。由于该证言基于被告的第一手认知——即她对自己所给付现金数额的记忆——因此是可采纳的。

（选项B）被告的证言是可采纳的——无论该账本是否由原告（对方当事人）提供——因为该证言具有关联性，并且基于她的亲身认知。

（选项C）采纳性承认 (an adoptive admission) 是一项传闻证据规则的例外，它允许采纳对方当事人已采纳为己有的他人陈述。因此，如果一个理性的人在相同情况下会提出质疑，那么被告未能对账本的准确性提出质疑，就可能构成采纳性承认。但该规则并不排除被告提供证言来反驳账本内容的可能性。

（选项D）最佳证据规则 (The best evidence rule) 通常要求，为了证明其内容，必须采纳原始的书面文件、录音或照片（例如，本案中的账本）。但该规则不影响旨在反驳账本内容的被告证言的可采纳性。

教学目标：一名非专业证人通常可以就任何相关事项作证，只要该证言是基于证人的亲身认知，或是基于此类认知而合理形成的常识性观感。

References

Fed. R. Evid. 602 (personal knowledge requirement).

Fed. R. Evid. 701 (opinion testimony by lay witnesses).

MBE 考点解析

证据法 (Evidence) - 证人证言
⚖️ 核心规则：亲身认知 (Personal Knowledge) 根据《联邦证据规则》第602条 (FRE 602)，非专家证人（Lay Witness）只能就其拥有亲身认知 (Personal Knowledge) 的事项作证。

只要证人是基于自己的感官（看、听、做）经历了某事，该证言通常就是可采纳的。
✅ 为什么选 A？

本题的关键在于区分“证明文件的内容”与“证明独立发生的事实”。

  • 被告（Defendant）并不是在朗读账本（Ledger）里的内容。
  • 被告是在回忆她亲手给钱这一行为。
  • 这是一个独立于账本之外发生的历史事实。被告作为给钱的人，对“给了多少钱”拥有第一手的亲身认知 (Firsthand Knowledge)。

因此，无论账本上写了什么，被告都有权根据自己的记忆作证。

⚠️ 常见陷阱：最佳证据规则
选项 D 错误

这是本题最大的干扰项。考生常误以为只要涉及记录，就必须以记录为准。

最佳证据规则 (Best Evidence Rule, FRE 1002) 仅在以下两种情况适用：

  1. 证据本身就是书面文件（例如：证明遗嘱的内容）；或者
  2. 证人对事实的唯一认知来源是该文件（例如：证人没去过现场，只是读了报告）。

破题技巧：在本案中，给钱这个动作是独立存在的。即使没有账本，给钱的事实依然发生过。被告不是在证明“账本里写了什么”，而是在证明“我实际给了多少钱”。因此，最佳证据规则不适用。

🚫 陷阱：采纳性承认
选项 C 错误

虽然被告没有反驳账本可能构成采纳性承认 (Adoptive Admission)，但这仅仅意味着账本可以作为证据被采纳（Admissible）。

关键点：承认 (Admission) 并不是结论性的 (Conclusive)。它不会封住被告的嘴。被告完全可以上台作证说：“是的，我当时没反驳，但我当时搞错了/没注意，实际上我给的钱更多。” 陪审团可以自行决定相信账本还是相信被告的证言。

🎓 考试贴士 (Exam Tip) 当题目问“证言是否可采纳”时，如果证人是事件的亲历者，优先考虑 FRE 602 (Personal Knowledge)。

不要让“文件存在”这一事实迷惑你，除非证人试图证明的是该文件的具体措辞。
MBE Evidence Q87098 Analysis
Based on Federal Rules of Evidence

questions.question:
A defendant was charged with murder. While walking down the hallway of the federal courthouse during a recess in the defendant's trial, the judge overheard the defendant say to his attorney, "So what if I did it? There's not enough proof to convict." After the judge reported the incident to counsel, the prosecutor called the judge as a witness in the trial.
Is the judge's testimony regarding the defendant's statement admissible?

choices.a: Yes, as the statement of a party-opponent.
choices.b: Yes, because the defendant's statement, although otherwise privileged, was made without reasonable efforts to preserve confidentiality.
choices.c: No, because the statement was a privileged attorney-client communication.
choices.d: No, because a judge may never testify in a trial over which he or she is presiding.

data.questionStem:
Q87113

A defendant was charged with murder. While walking down the hallway of the federal courthouse during a recess in the defendant's trial, the judge overheard the defendant say to his attorney, "So what if I did it? There's not enough proof to convict." After the judge reported the incident to counsel, the prosecutor called the judge as a witness in the trial.

Is the judge's testimony regarding the defendant's statement admissible?

一名被告被控犯有谋杀罪。在被告审判的休庭期间，当法官走在联邦法院的走廊上时，无意中听到被告对他的律师说：“就算我做了又怎样？没有足够的证据给我定罪。”法官将此事报告给双方律师后，检察官在审判中传唤法官作证。

法官就该被告陈述所作的证词是否可采纳？
options:
A. Yes, as the statement of a party-opponent.
是，因为这是对方当事人的陈述。

B. Yes, because the defendant's statement, although otherwise privileged, was made without reasonable efforts to preserve confidentiality.
是，因为被告的陈述，尽管本应享有特免权，但其作出时未采取合理措施来保持机密性。

C. No, because the statement was a privileged attorney-client communication.
否，因为该陈述是受特免权保护的律师-当事人间通讯。

D. No, because a judge may never testify in a trial over which he or she is presiding.
否，因为法官绝不能在其主持的审判中作证。
data.explanation:
Judge & juror competency as witness


JudgeMay not testify in trial over which judge is presiding No objection necessary to preserve issue for appeal
Juror
  • During trial
    May not testify before jury in which juror is sitting Objection outside jury's presence must be permitted
  • After trial or indictment
    May not testify about jury deliberations May testify about improper extraneous prejudicial information, outside influence, or mistake on verdict form
Under Federal Rule of Evidence 605, a judge is prohibited from testifying in a trial over which he/she is presiding. This is true even when that testimony pertains to otherwise admissible evidence - eg, statements by party-opponent, unprivileged communications. Therefore, the judge's testimony regarding the defendant's statement is inadmissible.

(Choice A) A statement made by a party-opponent (eg, the defendant) or his/her representative is generally admissible because it is not hearsay. But the statement cannot be admitted through the presiding judge's testimony.

(Choices B & C) Communications between a client and an attorney are privileged if they were intended to be confidential and made for the purpose of securing legal advice or representation. This privilege is not waived by an inadvertent disclosure to a third party (eg, the judge) unless the client failed to take reasonable steps to prevent or rectify the disclosure - eg, by communicating in a public place and loudly enough to be overheard (as seen here). But this does not allow a presiding judge to testify about the communication.

Educational objective: A judge may never testify in a trial over which he/she is presiding - even when that testimony pertains to otherwise admissible evidence.

选项正确率统计：A选项 1%，B选项 5%，C选项 2%，D选项 91%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

法官与陪审员作为证人的资格


法官不得在其主持的审判中作证，无需提出反对意见以保留上诉争议点
陪审员
  • 审判期间
    不得在自己所属的陪审团面前作证，必须允许在陪审团不在场时提出反对意见
  • 审判或起诉之后
    不得就陪审团的商议作证；可就以下事项作证：不当的、具有偏见性的外部信息，外部影响，或裁决书上的错误
根据《联邦证据规则》第605条 (Federal Rule of Evidence 605)，法官被禁止在其主持的审判中作证。即使该证词涉及其他可采纳的证据——例如，对方当事人的陈述、非特免权的通讯——这一规定也同样适用。因此，法官就该被告陈述所作的证词是不可采纳的。

(选项A) 由对方当事人（如被告）或其代表所作的陈述通常是可采纳的，因为它不属于传闻证据。但该陈述不能通过主审法官的证词来采纳。

(选项B和C) 当事人与其律师之间的通讯，如果意图是保密的并且是为了获得法律咨询或代理，则享有特免权。向第三方（如法官）的无意披露并不会导致此特免权的放弃，除非当事人未能采取合理措施防止或纠正该披露——例如，在公共场所进行沟通且声音大到足以被他人听到（如本案所示）。但这并不允许主审法官就该通讯内容作证。

教学目的：法官绝不能在其主持的审判中作证——即使该证词涉及在其他情况下可采纳的证据。

MBE 考点解析：法官作证资格

正确答案：D

本题考察的核心知识点是证人资格 (Competency of Witness)，具体涉及主审法官是否可以在其主持的案件中作证。

核心法规：Federal Rule of Evidence 605 (FRE 605) "The presiding judge may not testify as a witness at the trial. A party need not object to preserve the issue."

中文释义：主审法官不得在其主持的审判中作为证人作证。当事人无需提出异议即可保留该上诉争议点。

1. 法律推理 (Legal Reasoning)

根据 FRE 605，这是一个绝对的禁止性规定。无论法官要提供的证词内容是什么（即使该证词本身是可采纳的，例如被告的自白），只要该法官正在主持这场审判，他就绝对没有资格 (Incompetent) 坐上证人席。

背后的法理：

  • 公正性 (Impartiality)： 法官必须保持中立。如果法官作证，陪审团可能会给予法官的证词过高的权重。
  • 角色冲突： 对方律师无法在不冒犯法官或不显得对法庭不敬的情况下，对法官进行有效的交叉盘问 (Cross-examination)。

2. 为什么其他选项是错误的？

MBE 题目常设陷阱，让你关注证据的内容是否可采纳，而忽略了证人本身是否有资格。

选项 A (Hearsay Exception)：
虽然被告说 "So what if I did it?" 确实属于对方当事人陈述 (Statement of a Party-Opponent, FRE 801(d)(2))，通常不被视为传闻证据 (Hearsay)。但是，即使内容可采纳，也不能通过一个无资格的证人（法官）来引入。

选项 B & C (Privilege Issues)：
这两个选项都在讨论律师-当事人特免权 (Attorney-Client Privilege)。

  • 通常，在公共走廊大声说话会被视为放弃了保密性 (Waiver of confidentiality)，因此特免权可能确实不存在了（选项B的逻辑）。
  • 但是，这在本题中是次要问题。无论该对话是否享有特免权，主审法官都不能作证。FRE 605 的禁止是绝对的，优先于特免权的分析。

🎓 MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)
在处理证据法 (Evidence) 题目时，请遵循以下逻辑顺序：
  1. Competency (资格)： 证人能不能上台？（如本题：法官、陪审员通常不行）。
  2. Relevance (相关性)： 证据是否与案件有关？
  3. Admissibility Rules (可采性规则)： 是否存在 Hearsay、Privilege 或 Policy Exclusion 等排除规则？
如果第一步（资格）就不满足，后面的分析（如是不是传闻、是不是特免权）都是多余的。不要被复杂的证据内容规则分散注意力，先看谁在说话。

questions.question:
A defendant was charged with murder, and a witness testified for the prosecution. On cross-examination of the witness, the defendant seeks to elicit an admission that the witness was also charged with the same murder and that the prosecutor told her, "If you testify against the defendant, we will drop the charges against you after the conclusion of the defendant's trial."
Is the evidence about the prosecutor's promise to the witness admissible?

choices.a: No, because the evidence is hearsay not within any exception.
choices.b: No, because the law encourages plea-bargaining.
choices.c: Yes, as an admission by an agent of a party-opponent.
choices.d: Yes, as proper impeachment of the witness.

data.questionStem:
Q87096

A defendant was charged with murder, and a witness testified for the prosecution. On cross-examination of the witness, the defendant seeks to elicit an admission that the witness was also charged with the same murder and that the prosecutor told her, "If you testify against the defendant, we will drop the charges against you after the conclusion of the defendant's trial."

Is the evidence about the prosecutor's promise to the witness admissible?

一名被告被控犯有谋杀罪，一名证人为检方作证。在对该证人进行交叉询问时，被告试图引出证人的一项承认，即该证人也因同一谋杀案被起诉，并且检察官告诉她：“如果你作证指控被告，我们将在被告审判结束后撤销对你的指控。”

关于检察官对证人所作承诺的证据是否可采纳？
options:
A. No, because the evidence is hearsay not within any exception.
不可采纳，因为该证据是传闻证据，且不属于任何例外情况。

B. No, because the law encourages plea-bargaining.
不可采纳，因为法律鼓励辩诉交易。

C. Yes, as an admission by an agent of a party-opponent.
可采纳，因为这是对方当事人代理人的承认。

D. Yes, as proper impeachment of the witness.
可采纳，因为这是对证人的适当弹劾。
data.explanation:
Methods of impeaching witness


MethodDescriptionMeans
Character for truthfulnessReputation or opinion testimony
SIC involving bad act
SIC involving criminal conviction of felony or crime of dishonesty		Extrinsic evidence
Intrinsic evidence
Intrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Self-interest / biasMotive to lie or partiality to partyIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Prior inconsistent statementWitness's prior statement inconsistent with present testimonyIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Specific contradictionEvidence directly contradicting witness's testimony on material issueIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Sensory abilitiesEvidence showing witness's senses were impaired by physical / mental condition or environmental factorsIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
SIC = Specific instance of conduct.

A witness can be impeached (ie, discredited) with evidence of self-interest or bias - ie, something that may motivate the witness to testify falsely. Evidence of bias can be introduced intrinsically through the witness's own testimony OR extrinsically from any other source - including another witness's testimony.† Since a prosecutor's promise to drop pending charges may motivate a witness to testify falsely, evidence of the prosecutor's promise is admissible for impeachment purposes.

†The Federal Rules of Evidence do not require that a party lay a foundation by asking the witness about an alleged bias before introducing extrinsic evidence of that bias. However, many states' rules of evidence do (eg, Alaska, Texas).

(Choice A) Hearsay is an out-of-court statement offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted therein. Since the prosecutor's statement is being offered to show that the witness's testimony is motivated by self-interest - not to prove that the charges would actually be dropped if the witness testified favorably - it is not hearsay.

(Choice B) The law does encourage plea-bargaining - ie, a criminal defendant's agreement to plead guilty or no contest to a crime (not seen here) in exchange for some form of consideration from the prosecutor (eg, probation in lieu of jail time). But this does not provide a basis for excluding evidence.

(Choice C) Statements made by and offered against a party-opponent are not hearsay. This includes statements made by a party's agent on a matter within the scope of the agency relationship. Here, there is no evidence that the witness was the prosecutor's agent, so this is not a basis to admit the testimony.

Educational objective: Evidence that a witness's testimony was motivated by self-interest or bias is admissible to impeach the witness - ie, to discredit the truthfulness or reliability of the witness's testimony.

选项正确率统计：A选项 5%，B选项 11%，C选项 5%，D选项 77%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

弹劾证人的方法


方法描述方式
品格真实性声誉或意见证词
涉及不良行为的具体事例
涉及重罪或不诚实罪行的刑事定罪的具体事例		外部证据
内部证据
内部或外部证据
自身利益/偏见说谎的动机或对当事方的偏袒内部或外部证据
先前的矛盾陈述证人先前的陈述与本次证词不一致内部或外部证据
具体矛盾在实质性问题上直接反驳证人证词的证据内部或外部证据
感官能力证明证人感官因生理/心理状况或环境因素而受损的证据内部或外部证据
SIC = 具体行为事例。

证人可因自身利益或偏见的证据而被弹劾（即，被质疑其可信度）——即可能驱使证人作伪证的事情。偏见的证据可以通过证人自身的证词（内部证据）或任何其他来源（包括另一位证人的证词）引入（外部证据）。† 由于检察官承诺撤销待决指控可能会驱使证人作伪证，因此，检察官承诺的证据为弹劾目的而可被采纳。

†《联邦证据规则》(Federal Rules of Evidence) 不要求当事方在引入关于偏见的外部证据之前，通过询问证人有关其被指控的偏见来奠定基础。然而，许多州的证据规则确实有此要求（例如，阿拉斯加州、德克萨斯州）。

(选项 A) 传闻证据是指在庭外作出的、为证明其所述事项的真实性而提出的陈述。由于检察官的陈述是为了表明证人的证词是出于自身利益的动机——而不是为了证明如果证人作出有利证词，指控就真的会被撤销——因此它不构成传闻证据。

(选项 B) 法律确实鼓励辩诉交易——即刑事被告同意对某项罪行认罪或不抗辩（本案未见），以换取检察官的某种形式的对价（例如，以缓刑代替监禁）。但这并不构成排除证据的依据。

(选项 C) 由对方当事人作出并用于对抗该当事人的陈述不属于传闻证据。这包括当事人的代理人在代理关系范围内就某事项作出的陈述。在本案中，没有证据表明该证人是检察官的代理人，因此这不构成采纳该证词的依据。

教学目的： 证明证人证词是出于自身利益或偏见动机的证据，可用于弹劾该证人——即，质疑该证人证词的真实性或可靠性。

MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Impeachment & Bias
正确答案：D 可采纳，因为这是对证人的适当弹劾 (Proper Impeachment)。
⚖️ 核心法律规则解析

🎯偏见与自身利益 (Bias and Interest)

在证据法中，任何能够显示证人具有偏见 (Bias)、成见 (Prejudice) 或自身利益 (Interest) 的证据，对于评估证人的可信度都是至关重要的。

本案中，检察官承诺“如果你作证，我们就撤销对你的谋杀指控”。这给了证人一个巨大的撒谎动机（为了自保）。这种证据被称为显示偏见的证据 (Evidence of Bias)。

规则：显示偏见的证据总是相关的，并且可以被采纳用于弹劾证人。

🗣️传闻证据的陷阱 (The Hearsay Trap)

许多考生会误选 A，认为检察官的话是庭外陈述，属于传闻 (Hearsay)。

为什么不是传闻？

传闻必须是“为了证明所述事项的真实性” (Offered for the truth of the matter asserted)。

  • 被告引入这句话，不是为了证明检察官真的会撤销指控。
  • 而是为了证明这句话对证人心理产生的影响 (Effect on the listener)——即证人认为只要作证就能脱罪，因此有了撒谎的动机。

既然不是为了证明内容的真实性，它就不受传闻规则的限制。

❌ 为什么其他选项错误？
选项 A (传闻): 错误。如上所述，该陈述用于证明证人的动机（听者的反应），而非陈述内容的真实性，因此不是传闻。
选项 B (辩诉交易): 错误。虽然公共政策鼓励辩诉交易 (Plea Bargaining)，但这并不意味着可以向陪审团隐瞒证人与检方达成的交易。相反，为了保障被告的对质权 (Confrontation Clause)，必须允许被告揭露证人的潜在偏见。
选项 C (代理人承认): 错误。虽然检察官是政府的代表，但该证据的可采性基础是“弹劾偏见”，而非“对方当事人承认”。此外，证人本身通常不被视为检察官的代理人 (Agent)。即使这被视为一种承认，选项 D 也是更直接、更准确的理由。

💡 MBE 考试技巧 (Exam Tip)

在处理弹劾 (Impeachment) 问题时，请记住：

偏见 (Bias) 永远不是“附带问题” (Collateral Matter)。

这意味着，如果证人在交叉询问中否认了偏见（例如否认有交易），你不仅可以问，还可以引入外部证据 (Extrinsic Evidence) 来证明这一偏见的存在。这是 MBE 考试中非常喜欢考察的一个例外点。

questions.question:
A defendant is on trial in federal court for bank robbery. The prosecutor called a witness who testified that, while in the bank parking lot, she (1) saw the defendant and his accomplice running out of the bank while removing their ski masks and (2) heard the accomplice call the defendant by name as they ran to their red car.
Which of the following areas of questioning most likely exceeds the proper scope of cross-examination?

choices.a: A plane passed loudly overhead as the defendant and his accomplice ran to their car.
choices.b: The witness failed to report income on her federal tax returns for the past five years.
choices.c: The witness has suffered from colorblindness since childhood.
choices.d: The witness is a former alcoholic who regularly attends addiction support meetings.

data.questionStem:
Q87817 A defendant is on trial in federal court for bank robbery. The prosecutor called a witness who testified that, while in the bank parking lot, she (1) saw the defendant and his accomplice running out of the bank while removing their ski masks and (2) heard the accomplice call the defendant by name as they ran to their red car.

Which of the following areas of questioning most likely exceeds the proper scope of cross-examination? 一名被告因银行抢劫案在联邦法院接受审判。检察官传唤了一名证人，该证人作证称，在银行停车场时，她 (1) 看到被告及其共犯摘下其滑雪面罩跑出银行，并且 (2) 听到共犯在他们跑向一辆红色汽车时喊了被告的名字。

以下哪个提问领域最有可能超出交叉询问的适当范围？
options:
A. A plane passed loudly overhead as the defendant and his accomplice ran to their car.
当被告及其共犯跑向他们的汽车时，一架飞机从头顶大声飞过。

B. The witness failed to report income on her federal tax returns for the past five years.
在过去五年里，该证人未在其联邦纳税申报表上申报收入。

C. The witness has suffered from colorblindness since childhood.
该证人自童年起就患有色盲。

D. The witness is a former alcoholic who regularly attends addiction support meetings.
该证人曾有酗酒史，并定期参加戒瘾互助会。
data.explanation:
Under Federal Rule of Evidence (FRE) 611, the scope of cross-examination is limited to:

the subject matter of direct examination and matters affecting the witness's credibility.

One method of attacking a witness's credibility is to establish that, at the time in question, the witness's sensory abilities were impaired by a physical or mental condition or affected by environmental factors.

Here, the witness's testimony that she heard the accomplice call the defendant's name can be attacked with evidence that a plane was passing loudly overhead (Choice A). And the witness's testimony that she saw the defendant and his accomplice running to a red car can be attacked with evidence of her colorblindness (Choice C). Therefore, these areas of questioning are within the proper scope of cross-examination.

Another method of attacking a witness's credibility is to introduce specific instances of conduct (SICs) that are probative of the witness's character for truthfulness. SICs can always be introduced intrinsically—ie, by questioning the witness being impeached about the SIC. Therefore, questioning the witness about her failure to report income on her tax returns is also within the proper scope of cross-examination (Choice B).

However, a witness's alcoholism or drug addiction does not bear on the witness's truthfulness. And such addiction cannot be used to challenge the witness's sensory abilities unless the addiction affected the witness's memory or sensory perception at the time in question or while testifying. This protects the witness from undue harassment. Therefore, questions about the witness's alcoholism likely exceed the scope of cross-examination.

Educational objective: Evidence that a witness's senses were impaired by a physical or mental condition or by environmental factors at the time in question can be used to attack the witness's credibility. Specific instances of conduct probative of the witness's truthfulness may also be used, but a witness's addiction typically cannot.



根据《联邦证据规则》(FRE) 第611条，交叉询问的范围限于：

直接询问的主题事项以及 影响证人可信度的事项。

攻击证人可信度的一种方法是，证明在涉案之时，证人的感知能力因身体或精神状况而受损，或受到环境因素的影响。

在本案中，证人作证称她听到共犯喊被告的名字，这一点可以通过一架飞机从头顶大声飞过的证据来攻击（选项A）。而证人作证称她看到被告及其共犯跑向一辆红色汽车，这一点可以通过其色盲的证据来攻击（选项C）。因此，这些提问领域属于交叉询问的适当范围。

攻击证人可信度的另一种方法是，引入对证人的诚实品格具有证明力的特定行为事例 (SICs)。特定行为事例总可以通过内在方式引入——即，通过就该特定行为事例询问被弹劾的证人。因此，就证人未在纳税申报表上申报收入一事进行提问，也属于交叉询问的适当范围（选项B）。

然而，证人的酗酒或毒瘾问题与其诚实性无关。并且，除非该成瘾问题在涉案之时或作证时影响了证人的记忆力或感知能力，否则不得用此来质疑证人的感知能力。这是为了保护证人免受不当骚扰。因此，关于证人酗酒史的问题很可能超出了交叉询问的范围。

教学目标： 证人在涉案之时的感知能力因身体或精神状况或因环境因素而受损的证据，可用于攻击证人的可信度。对证人诚实性具有证明力的特定行为事例也可使用，但证人的成瘾问题通常不能。

References

Fed. R. Evid. 611 (scope of cross-examination).

Fed. R. Evid. 608(b) (impeachment through a witness's specific instance of conduct).

Christopher B. Mueller et al., 3 Federal Evidence § 6:80 (4th ed. 2021) (discussing when drug or alcohol addiction can be used to attack the witness's credibility).

MBE 证据法考点解析

Scope of Cross-Examination (FRE 611)
正确答案：选项 D

关于“证人曾有酗酒史并定期参加戒瘾互助会”的提问最有可能超出交叉询问的适当范围。

核心考点：FRE 611 & 弹劾 (Impeachment)

根据《联邦证据规则》(Federal Rules of Evidence, FRE) 第611(b)条，交叉询问的范围通常限于：

  1. 直接询问 (Direct Examination) 中涉及的主题事项；以及
  2. 影响证人可信度 (Credibility) 的事项。

本题的核心在于判断哪些问题属于合法的“弹劾证人可信度”。

为什么选项 D 超出范围？

D 超出范围 (Exceeds Scope)

分析：一般的酗酒史 (Alcoholism) 或毒瘾本身并不直接证明证人不诚实。除非有证据表明：

  • 证人在观察事件发生时处于醉酒状态（影响感知能力）；
  • 证人在出庭作证时处于醉酒状态（影响记忆或陈述能力）；
  • 成瘾导致了严重的精神损伤，影响了记忆力。

题目中提到证人是“前酗酒者 (former alcoholic)”且“定期参加互助会”，暗示其目前可能处于清醒状态。在没有证据表明其感知能力受损的情况下，询问此类隐私问题被视为骚扰 (Harassment) 或不当偏见，不属于合法的弹劾手段。

为什么其他选项是允许的？

A 允许 (Permissible)

感知缺陷 (Sensory Deficiency)
证人声称“听到”名字。飞机噪音直接挑战了其听觉感知能力。这是攻击证人是否真的能准确感知事实的标准方式。

C 允许 (Permissible)

感知缺陷 (Sensory Deficiency)
证人声称看到“红色”汽车。色盲 (Colorblindness) 直接挑战了其视觉感知能力及描述细节的准确性。这属于典型的弹劾感知能力。

B 允许 (Permissible)

FRE 608(b) 特定行为 (Specific Instances of Conduct)
根据 FRE 608(b)，在交叉询问中，可以询问证人关于诚实性 (Character for Truthfulness) 的特定行为。税务欺诈 (Tax Fraud) 涉及欺骗和隐瞒，直接关系到证人是否诚实。虽然不能引入外部证据 (Extrinsic Evidence) 来证明这一点，但允许在交叉询问中提问。

🎓 MBE 备考策略：

遇到涉及“证人成瘾 (Addiction)”的题目时，请寻找时间联系 (Temporal Nexus)。

如果题目没有说明证人在案发时或作证时受到毒品/酒精影响，仅仅因为某人是“瘾君子”通常不能用来弹劾其可信度。法院倾向于保护证人免受与其证词无关的羞辱。

questions.question:
A defendant was charged with possession of marijuana with intent to distribute. On direct examination, the defendant testified that he worked with disadvantaged children as a drug counselor, that he hated drugs, that he would "never possess or distribute drugs," and that he had never used drugs and would not touch them.
The government offered as a rebuttal witness a police officer who would testify that, three years earlier, she saw the defendant buy cocaine from a street dealer. The defendant objected.
Is the testimony of the police officer about the prior drug transaction admissible to impeach the defendant?

choices.a: No, because it is contradiction on a collateral matter.
choices.b: No, because the bad act of buying drugs is not sufficiently probative of a witness's character for truthfulness.
choices.c: Yes, because it is proper contradiction.
choices.d: Yes, because the bad act shows a disregard for the law and makes it less likely that the defendant would respect the oath of truthfulness.

data.questionStem:
Q87126

A defendant was charged with possession of marijuana with intent to distribute. On direct examination, the defendant testified that he worked with disadvantaged children as a drug counselor, that he hated drugs, that he would "never possess or distribute drugs," and that he had never used drugs and would not touch them.

The government offered as a rebuttal witness a police officer who would testify that, three years earlier, she saw the defendant buy cocaine from a street dealer. The defendant objected.

Is the testimony of the police officer about the prior drug transaction admissible to impeach the defendant?

一名被告被指控持有大麻并意图分销。在直接询问中，被告作证称，他作为一名戒毒顾问，与弱势儿童一起工作，他憎恨毒品，他“绝不会持有或分销毒品”，并且他从未使用过毒品，也不会碰它们。

政府提供了一名警官作为反驳证人，该警官将作证称，三年前，她看到被告从一名街头毒贩那里购买可卡因。被告提出反对。

该警官关于先前毒品交易的证词是否可采纳，以弹劾被告？
options:
A. No, because it is contradiction on a collateral matter.
不可以，因为这是对附带事项的反驳。

B. No, because the bad act of buying drugs is not sufficiently probative of a witness's character for truthfulness.
不可以，因为购买毒品的不良行为不足以证明证人具有诚信的品格。

C. Yes, because it is proper contradiction.
可以，因为这是适当的反驳。

D. Yes, because the bad act shows a disregard for the law and makes it less likely that the defendant would respect the oath of truthfulness.
可以，因为该不良行为表明了对法律的漠视，并使得被告遵守诚信誓言的可能性降低。
data.explanation:
Methods of impeaching witness


MethodDescriptionMeans
Character for truthfulnessReputation or opinion testimony
SIC involving bad act
SIC involving criminal conviction of felony or crime of dishonesty		Extrinsic evidence
Intrinsic evidence
Intrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Self-interest / biasMotive to lie or partiality to partyIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Prior inconsistent statementWitness's prior statement inconsistent with present testimonyIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Specific contradictionEvidence directly contradicting witness's testimony on material issueIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Sensory abilitiesEvidence showing witness's senses were impaired by physical / mental condition or environmental factorsIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
SIC = Specific instance of conduct.

A witness may be impeached (ie, discredited) with evidence that contradicts his/her testimony. This can be done by introducing either:
  • intrinsic evidence - testimony elicited from that witness on cross-examination or
  • extrinsic evidence - evidence elicited from any source other than that witness.

But under the collateral-evidence rule, extrinsic evidence cannot be used to impeach a witness on a collateral matter - ie, one that is irrelevant to a material issue in the case.

Here, the prosecution seeks to impeach the defendant-witness with the police officer's testimony that she saw him buy cocaine. Evidence of the prior cocaine purchase is not collateral since
  • the defendant-witness is charged with drug possession and
  • the evidence directly contradicts his testimony that he would "never possess or distribute drugs" (Choice A).
Therefore, the police officer's testimony is admissible to impeach him by contradiction.

(Choices B & D) Buying drugs is not probative of a witness's character for truthfulness. And even if it were, this specific instance of conduct involving a bad act could only be used to impeach a witness's truthfulness if it were introduced through intrinsic evidence. But here, the prior drug purchase is being used to impeach the defendant-witness by contradiction - not to attack his character for truthfulness - so it can be introduced through extrinsic evidence.

Educational objective: A witness may be impeached with evidence that contradicts his/her testimony. However, under the collateral-evidence rule, extrinsic evidence cannot be used to impeach a witness on a collateral matter.

选项正确率统计：A选项 7%，B选项 12%，C选项 73%（正确选项），D选项 6%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

弹劾证人的方法


方法描述方式
诚信品格声誉或意见证词
涉及不良行为的特定事例
涉及重罪或不诚实罪行的刑事定罪的特定事例		外在证据
内在证据
内在或外在证据
自身利益/偏见说谎的动机或对一方的偏袒内在或外在证据
先前的矛盾陈述证人先前的陈述与本次作证不一致内在或外在证据
具体反驳直接反驳证人就重要争议点所作证词的证据内在或外在证据
感知能力表明证人感知能力因身体/精神状况或环境因素而受损的证据内在或外在证据
SIC = 具体行为事例。

证人可能会因与其证词相矛盾的证据而被弹劾（即，削弱其可信度）。这可以通过引入以下任一方式实现：
  • 内在证据 - 在交叉询问中从该证人处引出的证词或
  • 外在证据 - 从该证人以外的任何来源引出的证据。

但根据附带证据规则，外在证据不能用于就附带事项——即与案件中重要争议点无关的事项——弹劾证人。

在本案中，控方试图用警官关于她看到被告购买可卡因的证词来弹劾作为证人的被告。先前购买可卡因的证据并非附带事项，因为
  • 作为证人的被告被控持有毒品，并且
  • 该证据直接反驳了他“绝不会持有或分销毒品”的证词（选项A）。
因此，该警官的证词可被采纳，以通过反驳的方式弹劾他。

（选项B和D）购买毒品并不能证明证人具有诚信的品格。即使可以，这种涉及不良行为的具体事例也只有在通过内在证据引入时，才能用于弹劾证人的诚信。但在这里，先前购买毒品的行为是用于通过反驳来弹劾作为证人的被告——而不是攻击其诚信品格——因此可以通过外在证据引入。

教学目标：证人可能会因与其证词相矛盾的证据而被弹劾。然而，根据附带证据规则，外在证据不能用于就附带事项弹劾证人。

References

Fed. R. Evid. 403 (excluding relevant evidence).
