data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence Law (证据法)
核心考点：具体反驳 (Specific Contradiction) 当证人在直接询问中做出全面性断言（Sweeping Assertion）时，对方可以使用外在证据（Extrinsic Evidence）来反驳该陈述，即使该事项原本可能被视为附带事项（Collateral Matter）。
案件逻辑分析

本题考察的是弹劾证人（Impeachment）中的一个特殊规则——“开门”理论 (Opening the Door)。

1. 被告的证词：
被告不仅仅是否认了当下的指控，他还做出了极端的、绝对化的陈述：他声称自己“绝不会持有或分销毒品”且“从未吸毒”。

2. 附带证据规则 (Collateral Evidence Rule)：
通常，如果一个问题与案件的核心事实无关（即附带事项），你不能引入外在证据（如传唤另一名证人）来证明证人撒谎，只能在交叉询问中质问。

3. 为什么本案可以引入外在证据？
当被告试图通过描绘自己是“憎恨毒品的反毒顾问”来证明自己无罪时，他将自己的“反毒历史”变成了案件的一个实质性争议点。此时，这不再是一个附带事项。

警官的证词直接反驳了被告“从未碰过毒品”的谎言。这种反驳被称为具体反驳 (Specific Contradiction)。

选项深度解析
✅ 选项 C (正确答案)
是的，因为这是适当的反驳。

被告的全面否认（Sweeping denial）为反驳证据“打开了大门”。警官的证词直接戳穿了被告在直接询问中建立的虚假人设，因此是可采纳的。

❌ 选项 A (错误)
理由：这并非“附带事项”。附带事项是指与案件核心无关的细枝末节。但在本案中，被告主动将“我从不碰毒品”作为其辩护的核心理由，因此反驳这一点就变成了实质性问题。
❌ 选项 B (错误)
理由：这是对 FRE 608(b) 的误用。虽然通常不能用“特定不良行为”的外在证据来攻击证人的诚实品格（Character for Truthfulness），但本题的依据是反驳 (Contradiction)，而不是攻击品格。当目的是反驳具体的谎言时，608(b) 的限制不适用。
❌ 选项 D (错误)
理由：这个选项试图利用“不良行为”来证明被告有犯罪倾向或不尊重法律，这接近于被禁止的“品格证据”推论（Propensity Argument），且逻辑不如选项 C 精确。
💡 MBE 考试技巧 注意区分 FRE 608(b) 和 具体反驳：
  • 如果控方只是想证明“他是个骗子，因为他以前买过毒品”，这是不允许用外在证据的（Rule 608）。
  • 如果被告说“我这辈子从未买过毒品”，控方证明“他买过”，这是允许用外在证据的（Contradiction）。
看到“Never”（从不）、“Always”（总是）这类绝对化词汇时，警惕“开门”规则的适用。
© MBE 备考助手 | 依据 Federal Rules of Evidence (FRE) 解析

questions.question:
A plaintiff sued a defendant for breach of a commercial contract in which the defendant had agreed to sell the plaintiff all of her requirements for widgets. The plaintiff called an expert witness to testify as to damages.
The defendant seeks to show that the expert witness had provided false testimony as a witness in his own divorce proceedings.
Should the defendant's evidence be admitted?

choices.a: No, because it is impeachment on a collateral issue.
choices.b: No, because it is improper character evidence.
choices.c: Yes, if elicited from the expert witness on cross-examination.
choices.d: Yes, if the false testimony is established by clear and convincing extrinsic evidence.

data.questionStem:
Q87069

A plaintiff sued a defendant for breach of a commercial contract in which the defendant had agreed to sell the plaintiff all of her requirements for widgets. The plaintiff called an expert witness to testify as to damages.

The defendant seeks to show that the expert witness had provided false testimony as a witness in his own divorce proceedings.

Should the defendant's evidence be admitted?

一名原告因被告违反商业合同而起诉该被告，在该合同中，被告同意向原告出售其所需的全部小部件。原告传唤一名专家证人就损害赔偿作证。

被告试图证明该专家证人在其本人的离婚诉讼中作为证人作证时曾提供虚假证词。

被告的证据是否应被采纳？
options:
A. No, because it is impeachment on a collateral issue.
不应采纳，因为这是对一个附带性争议点的弹劾。

B. No, because it is improper character evidence.
不应采纳，因为这是不当的品格证据。

C. Yes, if elicited from the expert witness on cross-examination.
应采纳，如果是在对专家证人进行交叉询问时引出的。

D. Yes, if the false testimony is established by clear and convincing extrinsic evidence.
应采纳，如果该虚假证词是由清晰且有说服力的外部证据所确立的。
data.explanation:
Methods of impeaching witness


MethodDescriptionMeans
Character for truthfulnessReputation or opinion testimony
SIC involving bad act
SIC involving criminal conviction of felony or crime of dishonesty		Extrinsic evidence
Intrinsic evidence
Self-interest / biasMotive to lie or partiality to partyIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Prior inconsistent statementWitness's prior statement inconsistent with present testimonyIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Specific contradictionEvidence directly contradicting witness's testimony on material issue
Sensory abilitiesEvidence showing witness's senses were impaired by physical / mental condition or environmental factors
SIC = Specific instance of conduct.

The defendant seeks to impeach the plaintiff's expert witness by attacking his character for truthfulness. This can be done by introducing extrinsic evidence - ie, evidence elicited from sources other than the expert's own testimony - to:
  • show the expert's reputation for untruthfulness
  • present another witness's opinion on the expert's truthful character
  • or prove a specific instance of conduct (SIC) involving a criminal conviction of a felony or crime of dishonesty.
But extrinsic evidence cannot be used to prove a SIC involving a prior bad act - ie, an illegal, immoral, or impermissible act that did not result in a criminal conviction. A bad act can only be introduced through intrinsic evidence - ie, evidence elicited during a witness's own testimony (usually on cross-examination) - if:
  • the bad act is probative of the witness's truthful character and
  • the inquiry into that bad act is made in good faith.
This is true even if the prior bad act (eg, the expert's false testimony) can be established by clear and convincing evidence (Choice D). Therefore, evidence of the expert's false testimony should be admitted if it is elicited from the expert on cross-examination.

(Choice A) The collateral-evidence rule prohibits the use of extrinsic evidence to impeach a witness on a collateral issue - ie, one that is irrelevant to the outcome of the case. But it does not apply here since intrinsic evidence would be used to impeach the expert and prior falsity is relevant to present credibility.

(Choice B) Character evidence is generally improper when it is used to show that a person acted in accordance with his/her character on the occasion at issue (ie, to prove liability). But it can be used for other purposes, like attacking a witness's credibility (as seen here).

Educational objective: A witness's character for truthfulness can be attacked by introducing a specific instance of conduct involving a prior bad act only on cross- examination if (1) the bad act is probative of the witness's truthful character and (2) the inquiry is made in good faith.

选项正确率统计：A选项 21%，B选项 14%，C选项 55%（正确选项），D选项 7%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

弹劾证人的方法


方法描述方式
关乎诚信的品格声誉或意见证词
涉及不当行为的特定事例
涉及重罪或不诚实罪行的刑事定罪的特定事例		外部证据
内部证据
利害关系/偏见说谎动机或对一方当事人的偏袒内部或外部证据
先前不一致的陈述证人先前的陈述与当前证词不一致内部或外部证据
具体矛盾在实质性争议点上直接反驳证人证词的证据
感官能力证明证人的感官因生理/心理状况或环境因素而受损的证据
SIC = 特定行为事例。

被告试图通过攻击原告专家证人关乎诚信的品格来弹劾该证人。这可以通过引入外部证据——即从专家自身证词以外的来源引出的证据——来实现，以：
  • 显示该专家的不诚信声誉
  • 提出另一名证人对该专家诚信品格的意见
  • 或证明涉及重罪或不诚实罪行的刑事定罪的特定行为事例 (SIC)。
但是，外部证据不能用于证明涉及先前不当行为的特定行为事例——即未导致刑事定罪的非法、不道德或不被允许的行为。不当行为只能通过内部证据——即在证人本人作证期间（通常是在交叉询问中）引出的证据——来引入，条件是：
  • 该不当行为对证人的诚信品格具有证明价值，并且
  • 对该不当行为的质询是出于善意进行的。
即使先前的不当行为（例如，专家的虚假证词）可以由清晰且有说服力的证据来确立，这一点也成立（选项D）。因此，如果专家提供虚假证词的证据是在交叉询问中从其本人处引出的，则该证据应被采纳。

（选项A）附带性证据规则禁止使用外部证据来弹劾一个关于附带性争议点（即与案件结果无关的争议点）的证人。但该规则在此处不适用，因为将使用内部证据来弹劾该专家，并且先前的虚假陈述与当前的可信度相关。

（选项B）当品格证据被用于证明某人在争议事件中依据其品格行事（即，证明法律责任）时，通常是不当的。但它可以用于其他目的，例如弹劾证人的可信度（如本案所示）。

教学目标：只有在交叉询问中，才能通过引入涉及先前不当行为的特定行为事例来攻击证人关乎诚信的品格，条件是 (1) 该不当行为对证人的诚信品格具有证明价值，并且 (2) 该质询是出于善意进行的。

References

Fed. R. Evid. 608(b) (impeaching witness's character for truthfulness).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Impeachment (证据法：弹劾证人)
⚖️ 核心考点：FRE 608(b) 关于特定行为事例 (Specific Instances of Conduct) 的规则：

为了攻击证人的诚实品格 (Character for Truthfulness)，在交叉询问 (Cross-examination) 中可以询问具体的“不当行为”事例，但严禁使用外部证据 (Extrinsic Evidence) 来证明该行为。
题目解析逻辑

本题考察的是如何利用“先前的不良行为”（Bad Acts）来弹劾证人的可信度。

1. 行为的相关性：
被告希望证明专家证人在之前的离婚案中作了伪证。作伪证（提供虚假证词）直接关系到一个人是否诚实，因此这与证人的诚实品格 (Character for Truthfulness) 高度相关。

2. 允许的方式（内部证据）：
根据 Federal Rules of Evidence (FRE) 608(b)，律师可以在交叉询问 (Cross-examination) 时直接问证人：“你是否在之前的离婚案中撒谎了？”这是允许的。

3. 禁止的方式（外部证据）：
如果证人否认撒谎，律师不能引入离婚案的庭审记录、也不能传唤另一位证人来证明专家撒谎了。这就是所谓的“禁止外部证据规则”。律师必须接受证人的回答（"Stuck with the answer"）。

选项分析
正确 C 应采纳，如果是在对专家证人进行交叉询问时引出的。

这是 FRE 608(b) 的直接应用。只要律师有善意基础 (Good faith basis) 相信证人撒谎了，就可以在交叉询问中提问。

错误 A 附带性争议点 (Collateral Issue)

虽然不能用外部证据证明附带问题，但证人的诚实度（Credibility）永远不是完全无关的。规则允许在交叉询问中“问”，只是不允许用外部证据“证”。选项 A 错误地完全排除了提问的可能性。

错误 B 不当品格证据 (Improper Character Evidence)

通常品格证据不能用来证明行为符合品格（Propensity），但这里是用于弹劾 (Impeachment)。攻击证人的诚实度是品格证据的合法用途之一。

错误 D 外部证据 (Extrinsic Evidence)

这是 MBE 最常见的干扰项！对于未导致刑事定罪的不当行为 (Bad acts not resulting in conviction)，永远不能使用外部证据，无论证据多么确凿（即使是 Clear and convincing）。

💡 考场实战技巧 (Exam Tip)

看到“Specific Bad Acts”（特定不良行为）用于弹劾时，请记住口诀：
"Ask, but don't prove." (可以问，不能证)

  • ✅ Cross-examination: OK (可以问)
  • ❌ Extrinsic Evidence: NO (不能拿文件、录音或其他证人来证明)
*注：除非该行为已经导致了刑事定罪 (Conviction)，那是 FRE 609 的范畴。

questions.question:
A defendant is charged with robbing a bank. The prosecutor has supplied the court with information from accurate sources establishing that the bank is a federally insured institution and that this fact is not subject to reasonable dispute. The prosecutor asks the court to take judicial notice of this fact. The defendant objects.
How should the court proceed?

choices.a: The court must take judicial notice and instruct the jury that it is required to accept the judicially noticed fact as conclusive.
choices.b: The court must take judicial notice and instruct the jury that it may, but is not required to, accept the judicially noticed fact as conclusive.
choices.c: The court may refuse to take judicial notice, because judicial notice may not be taken of essential facts in a criminal case.
choices.d: The court must refuse to take judicial notice, because whether a bank is federally insured would not be generally known within the court's jurisdiction.

data.questionStem:
Q87073

A defendant is charged with robbing a bank. The prosecutor has supplied the court with information from accurate sources establishing that the bank is a federally insured institution and that this fact is not subject to reasonable dispute. The prosecutor asks the court to take judicial notice of this fact. The defendant objects.

How should the court proceed?

一名被告被指控抢劫一家银行。检察官向法庭提供了来自可靠来源的信息，证明该银行是一家受联邦保险的机构，且此事实不存在合理争议。检察官请求法庭对此事实进行司法认知。被告提出反对。

法庭应如何处理？
options:
A. The court must take judicial notice and instruct the jury that it is required to accept the judicially noticed fact as conclusive.
法庭必须进行司法认知，并指示陪审团其必须接受经司法认知的事实为最终结论。

B. The court must take judicial notice and instruct the jury that it may, but is not required to, accept the judicially noticed fact as conclusive.
法庭必须进行司法认知，并指示陪审团其可以（但非必须）接受经司法认知的事实为最终结论。

C. The court may refuse to take judicial notice, because judicial notice may not be taken of essential facts in a criminal case.
法庭可以拒绝进行司法认知，因为在刑事案件中，不得对关键事实进行司法认知。

D. The court must refuse to take judicial notice, because whether a bank is federally insured would not be generally known within the court's jurisdiction.
法庭必须拒绝进行司法认知，因为银行是否受联邦保险并非法庭管辖区内普遍知晓的事实。
data.explanation:
Judicial notice of adjudicative facts (FRE 201)


Case typeTaking noticeInstructing jury
CivilCourt:
  • may take notice on its own
  • must take notice if party requests & supplies necessary information
Jury must accept noticed fact as conclusive
CriminalJury may accept noticed fact as conclusive
FRE = Federal Rule of Evidence

Judicial notice is a court's recognition of a fact as true without formal proof. Under Federal Rule of Evidence 201, the court may take judicial notice of any adjudicative fact that is not subject to reasonable dispute because it:
  • is generally known within the court's jurisdiction - ie, common knowledge in the community where the court is sitting or
  • can be accurately and readily determined from sources whose accuracy cannot reasonably be questioned (Choice D).

Judicial notice is mandatory if a party requests it and supplies the court with the necessary information to indicate that the fact is not subject to reasonable dispute. But in a criminal case, the jury cannot be instructed to accept a noticed fact as conclusive since this would impermissibly limit the defendant's right to a jury trial. Instead, the jury must be instructed that it may or may not accept the noticed fact as conclusive.†

Here, the prosecutor requested judicial notice of the fact that the bank is a federally insured institution. The court must notice this fact since the prosecutor supplied the court with information from accurate sources establishing that the fact is not subject to reasonable dispute. And since this is a criminal case, the court must instruct the jury that it may - but is not required to - accept the judicially noticed fact as conclusive (Choice A).

†Since a jury in a criminal case has the ability to pass upon judicially noticed facts, a court may not take judicial notice against a criminal defendant for the first time on appeal. However, a court may take judicial notice at any time, including on appeal, in all other proceedings.

(Choice C) A court may take judicial notice of essential facts (and other adjudicative facts) in a criminal case so long as those facts are not subject to reasonable dispute.

Educational objective:
A court must take judicial notice of a fact if a party requests it and supplies the court with the necessary information to show that the fact is not subject to reasonable dispute. And in a criminal case, the court must instruct the jury that it may or may not accept the noticed fact as conclusive.

选项正确率统计：A选项 11%，B选项 72%（正确选项），C选项 8%，D选项 8%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

对裁决事实的司法认知 (FRE 201)


案件类型进行认知指示陪审团
民事法庭:
  • 可自行决定进行认知
  • 如一方当事人提出请求并提供必要信息，则必须进行认知
陪审团必须接受经认知的事实为最终结论
刑事陪审团可以接受经认知的事实为最终结论
FRE = Federal Rule of Evidence (联邦证据规则)

司法认知是法庭无需正式证据即可认定某一事实为真实的做法。根据《Federal Rule of Evidence 201》，法庭可以对任何不存在合理争议的裁决事实进行司法认知，因为该事实：
  • 在法庭的管辖区内普遍为人所知——即，在法庭所在地的社区内属于常识 或
  • 能够通过其准确性不容合理质疑的来源进行准确、便捷的确定 (选项 D)。

如果一方当事人提出请求，并向法庭提供了必要信息以表明该事实不存在合理争议，那么进行司法认知是强制性的。但在刑事案件中，陪审团不能被指示必须接受经认知的事实为最终结论，因为这会不当地限制被告接受陪审团审判的权利。相反，必须指示陪审团，其可以接受也可以不接受经认知的事实为最终结论。†

在本案中，检察官请求对银行是受联邦保险的机构这一事实进行司法认知。法庭必须认知此事实，因为检察官已向法庭提供了来自可靠来源的信息，证明该事实不存在合理争议。并且，由于这是一起刑事案件，法庭必须指示陪审团，其可以（但非必须）接受经司法认知的事实为最终结论 (选项 A)。

†由于在刑事案件中，陪审团有权对经司法认知的事实进行裁决，因此法庭不得在上诉阶段首次作出对刑事被告不利的司法认知。然而，在所有其他程序中，法庭可在任何时候（包括上诉期间）进行司法认知。

(选项 C) 在刑事案件中，只要关键事实（及其他裁决事实）不存在合理争议，法庭可以对其进行司法认知。

教学目标：
如果一方当事人提出请求，并向法庭提供必要信息以证明某事实不存在合理争议，则法庭必须对此事实进行司法认知。在刑事案件中，法庭必须指示陪审团，其可以接受也可以不接受经认知的事实为最终结论。

References

Fed. R. Evid. 201 (judicial notice).

MBE 考点解析：司法认知
Judicial Notice (FRE 201)

核心考点： 在刑事案件中，法庭对事实进行司法认知后，陪审团的指示与民事案件截然不同。
第一步：判断是否应当进行司法认知

根据《联邦证据规则》第201条 (FRE 201)，如果一个裁决事实 (Adjudicative Fact) 不存在合理争议，法庭可以对其进行司法认知。不存在争议的标准有两个：

  1. 在管辖区内普遍知晓；或者
  2. 可以通过准确性不容置疑的来源迅速且准确地确定。

本题应用： 银行是否受联邦保险可以通过查阅官方记录（如FDIC记录）准确确定。检察官提供了可靠来源，且该事实无争议。当一方提出请求并提供必要信息时，法庭必须 (Must) 进行司法认知。

第二步：刑事案件中的特殊规则

这是本题的陷阱所在。虽然法庭必须认知该事实，但对陪审团的指示取决于案件类型。

案件类型 对陪审团的指示 (Jury Instruction)
民事案件
Civil Case		 陪审团必须接受该事实为最终结论。
(Must accept as conclusive)
刑事案件
Criminal Case		 陪审团可以（但非必须）接受该事实为最终结论。
(May accept as conclusive)

法律逻辑： 在刑事案件中，宪法第六修正案保障被告拥有由陪审团审判的权利。如果法官强制陪审团接受某个对定罪至关重要的事实（如银行受联邦保险），实际上等于法官在该要素上直接做出了裁决，这侵犯了被告的权利。因此，指示必须是许可性的 (Permissive)，而非强制性的。

为什么选 B？

因为检察官提供了充分的依据，法庭必须进行司法认知；同时因为这是刑事案件，法庭必须指示陪审团他们“可以”接受该事实，而不是“必须”接受。

其他选项错在哪里？
  • 选项 A： 错误。这是民事案件的标准。在刑事案件中强制陪审团接受事实是可逆转的错误。
  • 选项 C： 错误。法庭可以对构成犯罪要素的关键事实进行司法认知，只要该事实符合FRE 201的标准。
  • 选项 D： 错误。司法认知的标准是“普遍知晓”或“可准确验证”。虽然银行受保可能不是常识，但它是可以通过可靠来源验证的。
MBE 备考贴士： 看到 "Judicial Notice" 题目，第一时间圈出是 Civil 还是 Criminal。这是解题的关键分水岭。

Should the court admit the evidence?

choices.a: No, because bias must be shown on cross-examination and not by extrinsic evidence.

data.questionStem:
Q87105

A woman sued a man for damages stemming from an automobile collision. At trial, the woman wishes to show by extrinsic evidence that the man's primary witness is also his partner in a small-scale marijuana growing operation.

Should the court admit the evidence?

一名女性因一场车祸向一名男性提起损害赔偿诉讼。在审判中，该女性希望通过外来证据（extrinsic evidence）证明，该男性的主要证人也是他在一个小型大麻种植业务中的合伙人。

法院是否应该采纳该证据？
options:
A. No, because bias must be shown on cross-examination and not by extrinsic evidence.
不应该，因为偏见必须在交叉询问中展示，而非通过外来证据。

B. No, because the evidence would be more prejudicial than probative.
不应该，因为该证据的偏见性大于其证明力。

C. Yes, as evidence of the witness's character.
应该，作为证人品格的证据。

D. Yes, as evidence of the witness's possible bias in favor of the man.
应该，作为证人可能偏袒该男性的证据。
data.explanation:
Methods of impeaching witness


MethodDescriptionMeans
Character for truthfulnessReputation or opinion testimony
SIC involving bad act
SIC involving criminal conviction of felony or crime of dishonesty		Extrinsic evidence
Intrinsic evidence
Self-interest / biasMotive to lie or partiality to partyIntrinsic or extrinsic evidence
Prior inconsistent statementWitness's prior statement inconsistent with present testimony
Specific contradictionEvidence directly contradicting witness's testimony on material issue
Sensory abilitiesEvidence showing witness's senses were impaired by physical / mental condition or environmental factors
SIC = Specific instance of conduct.

A party may attack a witness's credibility by offering evidence that the witness is biased and therefore had a motive to lie while testifying. One method of establishing bias is showing that the witness is affiliated with the opposing party outside the context of the litigation. This can be established through either:
  • intrinsic evidence - by questioning the witness about the affiliation or
  • extrinsic evidence - by introducing the affiliation using any source other than the witness's testimony (Choice A).
Here, the woman seeks to introduce extrinsic evidence that the man's primary witness is also his partner in a small-scale marijuana growing operation. Since that affiliation is evidence of the witness's possible bias in favor of the man, the court should admit the evidence.

(Choice B) Relevant evidence may be excluded if its probative value is substantially outweighed by a danger of unfair prejudice - ie, a danger that the jury may decide the case on improper grounds. Here, the evidence poses some danger that the jury may side against the man because he grows marijuana. But that danger does not outweigh the evidence's probative value since it speaks directly to the witness's bias.

(Choice C) A witness's character for truthfulness becomes relevant when the witness takes the stand to testify, so a party may attack the witness's character - eg, by cross-examining the witness about specific instances of conduct that bear on the witness's truthfulness. But here, the woman seeks to establish the witness's bias, not to attack the witness's general character for truthfulness.

Educational objective: One method of establishing bias is showing that the witness is affiliated with the opposing party outside the context of the litigation. Such affiliation can be established through intrinsic or extrinsic evidence.

选项正确率统计：A选项 16%，B选项 13%，C选项 0%，D选项 69%（正确选项）
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

弹劾证人的方法


方法描述途径
有关诚信的品格声誉或意见证词
涉及不良行为的具体事例（SIC）
涉及重罪或不诚实罪行的刑事定罪的具体事例（SIC）		外来证据
内在证据
自身利益/偏见说谎的动机或对一方的偏袒内在或外来证据
先前不一致的陈述证人先前与当前证词不一致的陈述
具体矛盾在重要问题上直接与证人证词相矛盾的证据
感知能力证明证人感官因生理/心理状况或环境因素受损的证据
SIC = 具体行为事例（Specific instance of conduct）。

一方当事人可以通过提供证据来攻击证人的可信度，证明证人存在偏见，因此在作证时有说谎的动机。证明偏见的一种方法是，表明证人在诉讼背景之外与对方当事人有关联。这可以通过以下任一方式证明：
  • 内在证据 - 通过就该关联向证人提问或
  • 外来证据 - 通过使用除证人证词以外的任何来源来引入该关联（选项A）。
在本案中，该女性试图引入外来证据，证明该男性的主要证人也是他在一个小型大麻种植业务中的合伙人。由于该关联是证人可能偏袒该男性的证据，法院应当采纳该证据。

（选项B）如果相关证据的证明价值被不公正偏见的风险实质性地超过，则该证据可能被排除——即，陪审团可能基于不当理由对案件作出裁决的风险。在本案中，该证据带来了一定的风险，即陪审团可能因为该男性种植大麻而对他产生不利看法。但这种风险并未超过该证据的证明价值，因为它直接关系到证人的偏见。

（选项C）当证人出庭作证时，其有关诚信的品格就变得具有相关性，因此一方当事人可以攻击证人的品格——例如，通过就影响证人诚信的具体行为事例对证人进行交叉询问。但在本案中，该女性旨在证明证人的偏见，而非攻击其总体的诚信品格。

教学目标：证明偏见的一种方法是，表明证人在诉讼背景之外与对方当事人有关联。这种关联可以通过内在证据或外来证据来证明。

MBE 证据法精讲

Evidence: Impeachment by Bias

考点：证人弹劾 (Impeachment)

本题考察的是证据法中一个非常核心的区别：如何证明证人的偏见 (Bias) 与 如何证明证人的不诚实品格 (Character for Truthfulness)。

⚖️ 核心法则 (The Golden Rule) 对于偏见 (Bias)，法律允许使用外来证据 (Extrinsic Evidence) 进行证明。

注意：这与攻击证人“不诚实品格”的特定行为（FRE 608(b)）不同，后者通常禁止使用外来证据。
逻辑推演

1. 识别证据目的：
原告试图引入证据表明证人与被告是“大麻种植合伙人”。这个证据的核心目的不是为了说证人是个坏人（品格），而是为了说明证人与被告有利益捆绑，因此有动机撒谎（偏见）。

2. 偏见的可采性 (Admissibility of Bias)：
根据美国最高法院在 United States v. Abel 中的原则，偏见总是相关的。证明偏见不需要局限于交叉询问 (Cross-examination)，如果证人否认或为了加强证明力，通过其他证人或文件（即外来证据）来证明这种关系是允许的。

3. FRE 403 平衡测试：
虽然“种植大麻”涉及非法行为，可能产生偏见 (Prejudice)，但这种共同参与非法活动的纽带极强地证明了证人对被告的忠诚度。其证明价值 (Probative Value) 在本案中通常被认为超过了不公正偏见的风险。

✅ 正确答案 D 的依据：
法院应当采纳该证据。因为这是为了展示证人可能偏袒被告 (Bias)。只要是用于证明 Bias，外来证据通常是允许的。
高频易混淆点：外来证据的使用
弹劾理由 是否允许外来证据？
偏见 (Bias) ✅ 允许
(本题考点)
不诚实的具体行为 (Specific Bad Acts)
(无定罪记录)		 ❌ 禁止
(仅限交叉询问)
刑事定罪 (Criminal Conviction) ✅ 允许
(需符合FRE 609)
为什么排除其他选项？
选项 A 错误：它混淆了规则。只有在攻击“不诚实品格”的具体行为（FRE 608(b)）时，才限制只能在交叉询问中提及，不能引入外来证据。对于 Bias，没有此限制。
选项 B 错误：虽然大麻种植有偏见性，但在证据法中，展示证人与当事人共同参与“秘密也许是非法的”活动，是证明其紧密关系（即撒谎动机）的强有力证据。法院通常不会因此排除它。
选项 C 错误：这不仅是品格证据，而且如果是为了证明品格（Character），通常不允许用这种具体的非法行为（未定罪）的外来证据来证明。只有将其定性为“偏见”证据，才能通过外来证据引入。

questions.question:
A defendant was charged with possession of a prohibited firearm after a sawed-off shotgun was found in his vehicle during a routine traffic stop. At trial, the prosecutor called the officer who stopped the defendant's vehicle and questioned him about the basis for the traffic stop and the subsequent discovery of the shotgun. Thereafter, the defendant's attorney cross-examined the officer. To clarify the officer's testimony, the court then asked the officer several questions about the discovery of the shotgun that had not been asked by either party. The court excused the officer after giving each attorney a chance for further examination.
Later, while the jury was on its lunch break, the defendant's attorney objected to the court's questioning of the officer. The attorney requested that the court's examination be stricken from the record and that the jury be instructed to disregard it. The court overruled the objection and denied the request. The defendant was subsequently convicted. On appeal, the defendant argues that the court's questioning of the officer was improper.
Is the court of appeals likely to overturn the defendant's conviction on this basis?

choices.a: No, because a trial court may examine a witness for the purpose of clarifying the witness's testimony.
choices.b: No, because the defendant's attorney failed to timely object to the court's questioning of the officer.
choices.c: Yes, because in order to maintain neutrality, a trial judge may not examine a witness.
choices.d: Yes, because the court did not give the defendant notice of its intent to examine the officer.

一名被告在一次例行交通拦截中，其车内被发现藏有一支短管霰弹枪，后被控持有违禁枪支。庭审中，检察官传唤了拦截被告车辆的警官，并就交通拦截的依据及随后发现霰弹枪的过程对他进行了询问。此后，被告律师对该警官进行了交叉询问。为澄清警官的证词，法庭接着就双方当事人均未问及的有关发现霰弹枪的一些问题，向该警官进行了询问。法庭在给予双方律师进一步询问的机会后，让该警官退庭。

之后，在陪审团午休期间，被告律师对法庭询问警官的行为提出异议。该律师请求将法庭的询问从记录中删除，并指示陪审团不予理会。法庭驳回了该异议并拒绝了该请求。被告随后被定罪。被告在上诉中辩称，法庭对警官的询问是不当的。

上诉法院是否可能因此推翻被告的定罪？
options:
A. No, because a trial court may examine a witness for the purpose of clarifying the witness's testimony.
不会，因为审判法院可以为了澄清证人证词而询问证人。

B. No, because the defendant's attorney failed to timely object to the court's questioning of the officer.
不会，因为被告律师未能就法庭对警官的询问及时提出异议。

C. Yes, because in order to maintain neutrality, a trial judge may not examine a witness.
会，因为为保持中立，审判法官不得询问证人。

D. Yes, because the court did not give the defendant notice of its intent to examine the officer.
会，因为法庭未将其询问警官的意图通知被告。
data.explanation:
Court's authority over proceedings


(FRE 611, 614) Court has reasonable control over mode/order of examining witnesses & presenting evidence to:This allows court to:
  • effectively determine truth
  • avoid wasting time
  • protect witnesses from harassment or undue embarrassment
  • call witness upon its own motion or party's suggestion
  • examine witness, regardless of who called witness
FRE = Federal Rules of Evidence.

Federal Rule of Evidence (FRE) 611 grants the trial court control over the mode and order of presenting evidence and examining witnesses. This promotes the court's overarching duty to seek the truth. In furtherance of that duty, FRE 614 authorizes the court to develop or clarify testimony by:
  • calling a witness sua sponte or at the suggestion of a party and/or
  • examining a witness, regardless of who called the witness.


However, the court abuses this authority when it fails to grant all of the parties an opportunity to examine the witness or assume the role of an advocate.

Here, the officer was called by the prosecution and examined by both parties. The trial court then questioned the officer about the discovery of the shotgun to clarify his testimony, and the parties were given the opportunity to further examine him. There is no indication that the trial court assumed the role of an advocate, so the appellate court is not likely to overturn the defendant's conviction on this basis (Choice C).

(Choice B) An objection is generally timely if it is made at the earliest opportunity. But this rule is relaxed when a party seeks to object to the court's examination of a witness, and the objection may be postponed until the next opportunity that the jury is no longer present (as the defendant did here).†

†This saves the parties from any discomfort that may result from objecting to the court's questioning of a witness before the jury, while ensuring that the objection is raised in time for the court to implement corrective measures.

(Choice D) The court need not provide notice of its intent to examine a witness called by a party (as seen here). But notice should be given when the court intends to call a witness whom neither party intended to call so the parties can prepare to examine the witness. However, a conviction would only be overturned for failure to provide notice if it amounted to reversible error.

Educational objective: A court may both call a witness sua sponte or at the suggestion of a party and examine a witness to clarify or develop testimony. In doing so, the court may not deprive a party of the opportunity to examine the witness or assume the role of an advocate.

选项正确率统计：A选项 59%（正确选项），B选项 30%，C选项 7%，D选项 1%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

法庭对诉讼程序的权力


(FRE 611, 614) 法庭对询问证人和出示证据的方式/顺序拥有合理的控制权，旨在：这使得法庭可以：
  • 有效地查明真相
  • 避免浪费时间
  • 保护证人免受骚扰或不当的难堪
  • 依职权或根据一方当事人的建议传唤证人
  • 询问证人，无论其由哪一方传唤
FRE = Federal Rules of Evidence (联邦证据规则)。

《联邦证据规则》(Federal Rule of Evidence, FRE) 第611条授予审判法院对出示证据和询问证人的方式和顺序的控制权。这有助于法庭履行其寻求真相的首要职责。为履行该职责，FRE 614 授权法庭通过以下方式来完善或澄清证词：
  • 依职权（sua sponte）或应一方当事人的建议传唤证人，和/或
  • 询问证人，无论其由哪一方传唤。


然而，当法庭未能给予所有当事方询问证人的机会，或扮演一方代理人的角色时，即滥用此项权力。

在本案中，警官由检方传唤，并由双方当事人询问。审判法院随后就霰弹枪的发现过程询问了警官，以澄清其证词，且当事各方获得了进一步询问他的机会。没有迹象表明审判法院扮演了一方代理人的角色，因此上诉法院不太可能基于此理由推翻被告的定罪（选项C）。

（选项B）异议通常在最早的时机提出才算及时。但当一方当事人试图对法庭询问证人提出异议时，这条规则有所放宽，异议可以推迟到陪审团下一次不在场时提出（正如本案被告所做的）。†

†这使当事方免于因在陪审团面前对法庭的询问提出异议而可能导致的任何不适，同时确保异议被及时提出，以便法庭采取纠正措施。

（选项D）法庭无需就其询问一方当事人所传唤证人的意图发出通知（如本案所示）。但当法庭打算传唤任何一方当事人均无意传唤的证人时，则应给予通知，以便各方当事人能为询问该证人做准备。然而，只有在未给予通知构成可推翻判决的错误(reversible error)时，定罪才会被推翻。

教学目标：法庭既可以依职权或应一方当事人建议传唤证人，也可以为澄清或完善证词而询问证人。在此过程中，法庭不得剥夺一方当事人询问证人的机会，也不得扮演一方代理人的角色。

References

  • Fed. R. Evid. 611 (mode and order of examining witnesses and presenting evidence).
  • Fed. R. Evid. 614 (court's calling or examining of a witness).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence (证据法) - 法官询问证人的权力
正确答案：A

不会推翻定罪。因为初审法院（Trial Court）有权为了澄清证词而询问证人。

⚖️ 核心法律规则 (FRE 614)

根据《联邦证据规则》第614条 (Federal Rule of Evidence 614)：

  1. 传唤权：法庭可以依职权 (sua sponte) 或应一方请求传唤证人。
  2. 询问权：法庭可以询问任何证人，无论该证人是由哪一方传唤的。

目的：法官不仅仅是“裁判员”，更是“真相的寻求者”。只要是为了澄清证词 (clarify testimony) 或查明真相 (develop the truth)，法官的介入是允许的。

🔍 案情深度解析

在本案中，法官的行为完全符合 FRE 614 的规定：

  • 目的正当：法官提问是为了“澄清警官的证词”，这是为了帮助陪审团理解案情。
  • 程序公正：法官在提问后，给予了双方律师进一步询问 (further examination) 的机会，这消除了潜在的偏见。
  • 未丧失中立：题目明确指出法官只是为了澄清，并没有迹象表明法官扮演了“代理人/辩护人” (Advocate) 的角色或表现出偏袒。
❌ 为什么其他选项是错的？
选项 B (关于异议的及时性)：

这是一个极具迷惑性的选项。通常异议必须立即提出，但 FRE 614(c) 规定了一个例外：对法庭询问证人的异议，可以在陪审团下一次不在场时提出。

理由：这是为了避免律师被迫在陪审团面前公开反驳法官，从而导致尴尬或偏见。本案律师在午休（陪审团不在场）时提出异议，是及时的。

选项 C (关于中立性)：

法官必须保持中立，但这并不意味着法官必须保持沉默。只有当法官的提问表现出明显的偏见，实际上成为了检方的“代理人”时，才构成滥用裁量权 (Abuse of Discretion)。本案中仅是“澄清问题”，未越界。

选项 D (关于通知)：

法官询问已出庭的证人不需要提前通知。只有当法官决定传唤一个新的证人（特别是双方都没打算传唤的人）时，才通常需要通知，以便双方准备。

💡 MBE 拿分技巧

遇到“法官介入审判”的题目，请记住以下判断标准：

  • 允许：为了澄清困惑、管理时间、防止骚扰证人。
  • 禁止：表现出对被告有罪的看法、代替检察官进行盘问、剥夺一方律师的询问机会。
  • 异议时机：对法官行为的异议，只要在陪审团下一次离开法庭时提出，即视为及时。

questions.question:
A defendant is on trial for tax evasion. The defendant called his accountant to testify that the inconsistencies in the defendant's tax returns were clerical errors that occurred when the defendant's account information was transferred into a new accounting system. On cross-examination, the prosecutor seeks to attack the accountant's credibility by questioning him about his prior arrest for embezzlement and introducing evidence of his prior conviction for disorderly conduct.
If the defendant objects, how should the court rule?

choices.a: Admit evidence of the arrest and the conviction, because the witness opened the door to reputation testimony.
choices.b: Admit evidence of the arrest, but exclude evidence of the conviction because specific instances of conduct must be introduced intrinsically.
choices.c: Exclude evidence of the arrest and the conviction, but allow the prosecutor to cross-examine the accountant about the underlying conduct that led to the arrest.
choices.d: Exclude evidence of the conviction, but admit evidence of the arrest because it involves a crime of dishonesty.

data.questionStem:
Q87104

A defendant is on trial for tax evasion. The defendant called his accountant to testify that the inconsistencies in the defendant's tax returns were clerical errors that occurred when the defendant's account information was transferred into a new accounting system. On cross-examination, the prosecutor seeks to attack the accountant's credibility by questioning him about his prior arrest for embezzlement and introducing evidence of his prior conviction for disorderly conduct.

If the defendant objects, how should the court rule?

一名被告因税务欺诈案正在受审。被告传唤其会计师作证，称被告纳税申报表中的不一致之处，是在被告的账户信息转移至新会计系统时发生的笔误。在交叉询问中，检察官试图通过询问该会计师先前因挪用公款而被逮捕的记录，并引入其先前因妨害治安行为而被定罪的证据，来攻击该会计师的可信度。

如果被告提出异议，法院应如何裁决？
options:
A. Admit evidence of the arrest and the conviction, because the witness opened the door to reputation testimony.
采纳关于逮捕和定罪的证据，因为证人已为品格证据的引入打开了大门。

B. Admit evidence of the arrest, but exclude evidence of the conviction because specific instances of conduct must be introduced intrinsically.
采纳关于逮捕的证据，但排除关于定罪的证据，因为特定行为事例必须通过内在方式引入。

C. Exclude evidence of the arrest and the conviction, but allow the prosecutor to cross-examine the accountant about the underlying conduct that led to the arrest.
排除关于逮捕和定罪的证据，但允许检察官交叉询问该会计师关于导致其被捕的基础行为。

D. Exclude evidence of the conviction, but admit evidence of the arrest because it involves a crime of dishonesty.
排除关于定罪的证据，但采纳关于逮捕的证据，因为它涉及不诚实犯罪。
data.explanation:
Any party can impeach a witness with reputation or opinion testimony OR specific instances of conduct (SICs) that are probative of the witness's character for (un)truthfulness.† Only two types of SICs are admissible for this purpose: (1) convictions for a felony or crime of dishonesty and (2) other bad acts. A conviction for a felony or crime of dishonesty can be introduced:

intrinsically - through the witness's own testimony or extrinsically - through another witness's testimony or any other source.

In contrast, other bad acts can only be introduced intrinsically.

Here, the prosecutor seeks to introduce extrinsic evidence of the accountant's prior conviction for disorderly conduct. However, disorderly conduct is typically a misdemeanor offense that involves unruly behavior - not dishonesty. As a result, the prosecutor cannot use this conviction to impeach the accountant (Choice A). And though embezzlement is a crime of dishonesty, an arrest is not a conviction.

An arrest is also not a bad act because an arrest for misconduct is not itself misconduct. This means that the prosecutor cannot cross-examine the accountant about his prior arrest for impeachment purposes (Choices A, B & D). In contrast, the underlying conduct (ie, bad acts) that led to the embezzlement arrest can be used for impeachment purposes because that conduct is probative of the accountant's character for truthfulness.

†A witness's character for truthfulness may only be supported by reputation or opinion testimony after it has been attacked.

Educational objective: Specific instances of conduct involving a conviction for a felony or crime of dishonesty OR other bad acts can be admitted to impeach a witness's character for truthfulness. However, a mere arrest - as opposed to the underlying conduct leading to the arrest - is inadmissible for such purposes.



选项正确率统计：A选项 5%，B选项 8%，C选项 44%（正确选项），D选项 41%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

任何一方都可以通过品格或意见证言，或对证人的（不）诚实品格具有证明力的特定行为事例（SICs）来弹劾证人。† 为此目的，只有两种类型的特定行为事例是可采纳的：（1）重罪或不诚实犯罪的定罪记录，以及（2）其他不当行为。重罪或不诚实犯罪的定罪记录可以被引入：

内在方式 - 通过证人自己的证词 或 外在方式 - 通过另一位证人的证词或任何其他来源。

相比之下，其他不当行为只能通过内在方式引入。

在本案中，检察官试图引入该会计师先前因妨害治安行为而被定罪的外在证据。然而，妨害治安行为通常是一种涉及不守规矩行为的轻罪——而非不诚实行为。因此，检察官不能使用这一定罪记录来弹劾该会计师（选项A）。而且，尽管挪用公款是一种不诚实犯罪，但逮捕并非定罪。

逮捕本身也不是不当行为，因为因不当行为被捕本身并非不当行为。这意味着检察官不能为了弹劾的目的而就其先前的逮捕记录交叉询问该会计师（选项A、B和D）。相反，导致因挪用公款被捕的基础行为（即不当行为）可以用于弹劾目的，因为该行为对会计师的诚实品格具有证明力。

†证人的诚实品格只有在受到攻击后，才能通过品格或意见证言来加以支持。

教学目标：涉及重罪或不诚实犯罪的定罪记录，或其他不当行为的特定事例，可以被采纳以弹劾证人的诚实品格。然而，仅仅是逮捕记录——不同于导致逮捕的基础行为——为此目的是不可采纳的。

References

  • Fed. R. Evid. 608 (witness's character for truthfulness).
  • Fed. R. Evid. 609 (impeachment by evidence of criminal conviction).
  • Michelson v. United States, 335 U.S. 469, 482 (1948) (stating that an arrest without more does not impeach the integrity or impair the credibility of a witness).

MBE 考点解析

Evidence: Impeachment (弹劾证人)
正确答案：C

法院应排除关于逮捕和定罪的证据，但允许检察官交叉询问该会计师关于导致其被捕的基础行为（underlying conduct）。

考点一：逮捕记录不可用于弹劾

根据 FRE 608(b)，你可以询问证人关于其诚实品格的“特定行为事例”（Specific Instances of Conduct），但有严格限制：

  • 规则：仅仅被“逮捕”（Arrest）并不是一种不当行为。逮捕只是警方的指控，并不证明证人确实实施了该行为。
  • 例外：你可以询问导致逮捕的基础行为（Underlying Conduct）。
  • 应用：挪用公款（Embezzlement）涉及不诚实，对证人的可信度有证明力。因此，检察官可以问：“你是否曾经挪用公款？”（询问行为），但不能问：“你是否曾因挪用公款被捕？”（询问逮捕）。
考点二：定罪记录的筛选

根据 FRE 609，使用刑事定罪（Criminal Conviction）弹劾证人有明确门槛：

  • 不诚实犯罪 (Crimen Falsi)：无论重罪还是轻罪，只要涉及不诚实或虚假陈述（如伪证、欺诈、挪用公款），必须采纳。
  • 重罪 (Felony)：如果不涉及不诚实，法院需进行权衡测试（Rule 403 Balancing）。
  • 普通轻罪 (Misdemeanor)：如果不涉及不诚实，通常不可采纳。
  • 应用：本案中的“妨害治安”（Disorderly Conduct）通常是轻罪，且不涉及不诚实。因此，该定罪记录不可用于弹劾。
干扰项辨析
选项 A & D 错误： 它们主张采纳“逮捕”证据。如前所述，逮捕本身不能作为证据，只能询问基础行为。
选项 B 错误： 虽然它正确地指出了特定行为事例（SICs）通常通过内在方式（交叉询问）引入，但它错误地允许了“逮捕”证据的引入。此外，它错误地排除了定罪证据的理由（定罪证据其实可以通过外在证据引入，只是本案中的罪名不符合要求）。
💡 MBE 实战技巧

看到“Arrest”（逮捕）用于 Impeachment 时，请立即警惕：

  1. Arrest itself? NO.（不能直接问逮捕记录）
  2. Underlying Act? YES, if probative of truthfulness.（可以问导致逮捕的那个不诚实行为）
  3. Extrinsic Evidence? NO for bad acts (FRE 608).（对于未定罪的不当行为，不能引入外部证据，必须接受证人的回答）。
© MBE Evidence Review | Based on Federal Rules of Evidence

questions.question:
In a prosecution of a defendant for forgery, the defense objects to the testimony of a government expert on the ground of inadequate qualifications. The government seeks to introduce a letter from the expert's former criminology professor, stating that the expert is generally acknowledged in his field as well qualified.
On the issue of the expert's qualifications, who may properly consider the letter?

choices.a: Both the judge and the jury, because the letter is not offered for a hearsay purpose.
choices.b: Neither the judge nor the jury, because it is hearsay not within any exception.
choices.c: The judge, without regard to the hearsay rule.
choices.d: The jury, without regard to the hearsay rule.

data.questionStem:
Q87081

In a prosecution of a defendant for forgery, the defense objects to the testimony of a government expert on the ground of inadequate qualifications. The government seeks to introduce a letter from the expert's former criminology professor, stating that the expert is generally acknowledged in his field as well qualified.

On the issue of the expert's qualifications, who may properly consider the letter?

在一起针对某被告的伪造罪诉讼中，辩方以资格不足为由，反对一名政府方专家的证言。政府方试图引入一封来自该专家前犯罪学教授的信函，信中称该专家在其领域内被公认为具备充分资格。

关于专家资格的问题，谁可以适当地审议这封信函？
options:
A. Both the judge and the jury, because the letter is not offered for a hearsay purpose.
法官和陪审团均可，因为该信函并非为传闻证据目的而提供。

B. Neither the judge nor the jury, because it is hearsay not within any exception.
法官和陪审团均不可，因为该信函是传闻证据，且不属于任何例外情况。

C. The judge, without regard to the hearsay rule.
法官可以，无需考虑传闻证据规则。

D. The jury, without regard to the hearsay rule.
陪审团可以，无需考虑传闻证据规则。
data.explanation:
A witness is qualified to provide expert opinion testimony if the witness has specialized knowledge, skill, experience, education, or training in a subject that pertains to an issue in the case. Whether a witness meets these qualifications is a preliminary question for the court - not the jury. The court is not bound by the rules of evidence in deciding such questions.† Therefore, the court may consider otherwise inadmissible hearsay (eg, the professor's letter) in determining if a witness is qualified to provide expert opinion testimony (Choices A, B & D).

†The Federal Rules of Evidence typically apply to all civil and criminal proceedings before U.S. district courts, U.S. courts of appeal, U.S. bankruptcy courts, the U.S. Court of Federal Claims, and U.S. magistrate judges. Preliminary-question hearings are one exception to this rule.

Educational objective: Whether a witness meets the qualifications to offer expert opinion testimony is a preliminary question for the court - not the jury. The court is not bound by the rules of evidence when determining such questions.

选项正确率统计：A选项 13%，B选项 5%，C选项 75%（正确选项），D选项 5%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

如果证人对与案件争议点相关的某一主题拥有专业知识、技能、经验、教育或培训，则该证人有资格提供专家意见证言。证人是否满足这些资格是一个由法庭（即法官）而非陪审团决定的先决问题。在裁定此类问题时，法庭不受证据规则的约束†。因此，法庭在裁定证人是否有资格提供专家意见证言时，可以考虑在其他情况下不可采纳的传闻证据（例如，该教授的信函）(选项 A、B 和 D)。

†《Federal Rules of Evidence》通常适用于美国地区法院、美国上诉法院、美国破产法院、美国联邦索赔法院和美国联邦治安法官审理的所有民事和刑事诉讼程序。先决问题听证会是此规则的一项例外。

教学目标：证人是否满足提供专家意见证言的资格，是一个由法庭（即法官）而非陪审团决定的先决问题。在裁定此类问题时，法庭不受证据规则的约束。

References

Fed. R. Evid. 104 (preliminary questions).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 考点解析

Evidence Law: Preliminary Questions

⚖️ 核心考点：先决问题

本题考察的是证据法中的先决问题 (Preliminary Questions) 以及法官在决定证据可采性时的权力范围。

法律依据：FRE 104(a)
法庭（法官）必须裁定有关证人资格、特权是否存在或证据是否可采纳的先决问题。在作出此类裁定时，法庭不受证据规则的约束（特权规则除外）。
🔍 深度解析

为什么正确答案是 C？解析如下：

  • 问题本质： 辩方质疑专家的资格 (Qualifications)。证人是否有资格作为专家作证，属于证据可采性的先决问题。
  • 决策者 (Who)： 根据 FRE 104(a)，这类问题由法官 (Judge) 单独决定，而不是陪审团。
  • 规则适用 (How)： 法官在处理先决问题时，不受传闻证据规则 (Hearsay Rule) 等排他性规则的限制。

具体到本案：
虽然教授的信是典型的传闻证据 (Hearsay)（庭外陈述，用于证明专家有资格这一事实），在庭审中通常不可被陪审团采纳。但是，法官为了决定“该专家是否合格”这一程序性问题，可以阅读并参考这封信。

❌ 排除错误选项
  • 选项 A & D 错误： 陪审团 (Jury) 负责裁决案件事实，不负责裁定证据的可采性或证人的资格。此外，该信件对陪审团而言是不可采纳的传闻。
  • 选项 B 错误： 虽然信件是传闻，但 FRE 104(a) 明确规定法官在裁定先决问题时可以忽略传闻规则。因此说“法官不可审议”是错误的。
💡 考试技巧 (Exam Tips)

在 MBE 证据法题目中，区分 FRE 104(a) 和 FRE 104(b) 是拿分关键：

  • 法官决定 (Judge) - 104(a)： 证人资格、传闻例外、特权等。不受证据规则约束。（本题考点）
  • 陪审团决定 (Jury) - 104(b)： 有条件的相关性 (Conditional Relevance)。例如：证据A只有在证据B存在时才相关。法官只需看是否有足够的证据支持陪审团可能做出的认定。

记忆口诀：
"The Judge is the Gatekeeper." (法官是守门人，守门时可以看任何材料，除了特权材料。)

questions.question:
A witness for the prosecution in a murder case testified on direct examination that she saw the defendant and the victim in a heated argument at a local bar the same night the victim was murdered. When asked by the prosecutor what time she left the bar, the witness was unable to remember. The prosecutor seeks to show the witness his handwritten notes of the witness's pretrial interview during which she stated that she left the bar at 10:00 p.m.
How is the trial court likely to view the prosecutor's request to show the witness his notes?

choices.a: A proper attempt to introduce a recorded recollection.
choices.b: A proper attempt to refresh the witness's recollection.
choices.c: An improper attempt to lead the witness.
choices.d: An improper attempt to support the witness's credibility.

data.questionStem:
Q87120

A witness for the prosecution in a murder case testified on direct examination that she saw the defendant and the victim in a heated argument at a local bar the same night the victim was murdered. When asked by the prosecutor what time she left the bar, the witness was unable to remember. The prosecutor seeks to show the witness his handwritten notes of the witness's pretrial interview during which she stated that she left the bar at 10:00 p.m.

How is the trial court likely to view the prosecutor's request to show the witness his notes?

在一起谋杀案中，一名控方证人在直接询问中作证称，在受害者被谋杀的当晚，她看到被告和受害者在当地一家酒吧激烈争吵。当检察官问她何时离开酒吧时，证人无法记起。检察官试图向证人出示他在对该证人进行庭前访谈时所做的手写笔记，笔记中记载该证人曾陈述她于晚上10点离开酒吧。

审判法院可能会如何看待检察官向证人出示其笔记的请求？
options:
A. A proper attempt to introduce a recorded recollection.
为引入“存有记录的回忆”所作的正当尝试。

B. A proper attempt to refresh the witness's recollection.
为唤醒证人回忆所作的正当尝试。

C. An improper attempt to lead the witness.
为诱导证人所作的不正当尝试。

D. An improper attempt to support the witness's credibility.
为支持证人可信度所作的不正当尝试。
data.explanation:
A party may use any item (usually a writing) to refresh a witness's recollection when:

  • the witness once had personal knowledge of a fact or event but is now unable to recall it and
  • the item will help the witness recall that information.

Here, it is clear from the prosecutor's notes that the witness knew what time she left the bar during her pretrial interview and that viewing those notes would help her recall and testify to that time. Therefore, the court will likely view the prosecutor's request to show the witness his notes as a

proper attempt to refresh her recollection.

(Choice A) It would only be proper to admit the prosecutor's notes into evidence as a recorded recollection if the witness had reviewed the notes when the matter was fresh in her mind and been satisfied that they accurately reflected her knowledge. But the notes can be used to refresh her recollection without regard to their admissibility.

(Choice C) Leading questions are ones that suggest the desired response to the person being asked. Although these questions are generally prohibited on direct examination, using a writing or other item to refresh a witness's memory does not constitute leading the witness.

(Choice D) It is improper to offer evidence to support a witness's credibility before it has been attacked (ie, before the witness has been impeached). But here, the prosecutor's notes are being used to refresh the witness's memory - not to establish her credibility.

Educational objective: Any item may be used to refresh a witness's memory when (1) the witness once had personal knowledge of a matter but is now unable to recall it and (2) the item will help the witness recall that matter.



选项正确率统计：A选项 5%，B选项 81%（正确选项），C选项 11%，D选项 2%
正确率基于先前软件用户的统计（以美国本地法学生为主），仅供参考。

当事人可以使用任何物品（通常是书面文件）来唤醒证人的回忆，条件是：

  • 证人曾对某事实或事件有亲身认知，但现在无法回忆，并且
  • 该物品将帮助证人回忆起该信息。

在本案中，从检察官的笔记可以清楚地看出，证人在庭前访谈时知道她离开酒吧的时间，并且查看这些笔记将有助于她回忆并就该时间作证。因此，法院可能会将检察官向证人出示其笔记的请求视为

一次唤醒其回忆的正当尝试。

（选项 A） 只有在证人对事件记忆犹新时审阅过笔记，并确信笔记准确反映了其认知的情况下，将检察官的笔记作为“存有记录的回忆”采纳为证据才是正当的。但是，无论笔记是否具有可采纳性，都可以用它来唤醒她的回忆。

（选项 C） 诱导性问题是指向被询问者暗示所期望的回答的问题。尽管在直接询问中通常禁止使用此类问题，但使用书面文件或其他物品来唤醒证人的记忆并不构成诱导证人。

（选项 D） 在证人的可信度受到攻击（即，在证人受到弹劾）之前，提供证据来支持其可信度是不正当的。但在本案中，检察官的笔记是用来唤醒证人的记忆，而不是为了确立其可信度。

教学目标： 当（1）证人曾对某事项有亲身认知但现在无法回忆，且（2）某物品将有助于证人回忆起该事项时，任何物品都可以用来唤醒证人的记忆。

References

Fed. R. Evid. 612 (refreshing recollection).

data.htmlContent:
MBE 证据法考点解析

Presentation of Evidence
正确答案：B 法院会将其视为为唤醒证人回忆所作的正当尝试 (A proper attempt to refresh the witness's recollection)。
核心考点：唤醒记忆 (Refreshing Recollection)

本题考察的是联邦证据规则第612条（Fed. R. Evid. 612）。

法律规则：
当证人在作证时忘记了某个具体细节，律师可以使用任何物品（Any item/writing）来帮助证人恢复记忆。

操作步骤：

  1. 证人表示无法记起（Unable to remember）。
  2. 律师向证人展示物品（如笔记、照片、文件）。
  3. 证人默读或查看该物品。
  4. 律师收回物品。
  5. 证人表示记忆已恢复，并根据现在的记忆（Present memory）进行作证。

本案分析：
证人忘记了离开酒吧的时间。检察官拿出庭前访谈的笔记给证人看，目的是为了让她想起那个时间点，然后自己说出来。这完全符合“唤醒记忆”的程序。

关键区分：唤醒记忆 vs. 存有记录的回忆

这是MBE中最常见的陷阱之一，即混淆选项A和选项B。

特性 唤醒记忆
(Refreshing Recollection)		 存有记录的回忆
(Recorded Recollection)
规则 FRE 612 FRE 803(5)
目的 帮助证人想起来 证人实在想不起来，用记录代替证词
证据地位 文件不是证据（除非对方律师要求） 文件内容被宣读进记录（Read into evidence）
使用前提 证人忘记了 证人看过文件后仍然无法回忆起细节
为什么其他选项是错误的？
选项 A (Recorded Recollection) 错误：
这是传闻证据的例外（Hearsay Exception）。只有当证人看了笔记后依然无法回忆起内容时，才能试图引入笔记的内容。本题中，检察官只是刚开始展示笔记试图唤醒记忆，尚未达到引入“存有记录的回忆”的阶段。
选项 C (Leading) 错误：
诱导性问题（Leading Question）是指在问题中包含了答案（例如：“你是在晚上10点离开的，对吗？”）。仅仅向证人展示一份文件让她看，并不构成诱导性提问。
选项 D (Supporting Credibility) 错误：
虽然通常不能在证人被攻击前支持其可信度（Bolstering），但这里检察官的目的不是为了证明“她是个诚实的人”，而是为了获取“她几点离开”这一事实证据。
MBE 考试通关秘籍

看到“证人忘记了”(Witness forgets) + “律师拿东西给证人看”(Shows a writing)，首先想到的必须是 Refreshing Recollection。

只有当题目明确说“证人看了文件后说：‘我还是记不起来，但我当时写的肯定是准的’”时，你才应该考虑 Recorded Recollection (Hearsay Exception)。

questions.question:
An employer was sued by a former employee with hearing loss for failing to provide reasonable accommodations as required by federal law. At trial, the former employee's lawyer called the employer as a witness to testify as to the former employee's assigned tasks and the steps the employer had taken to accommodate the former employee. On cross-examination, the employer's lawyer asked the employer a question about an accommodation the employer had failed to mention: "Didn't you provide him with a smartphone so he could receive text messages about information that other employees received through a public address system?" The former employee's lawyer objected to the question as a leading question.
Can the court sustain the objection?

choices.a: No, because the employer was being cross-examined.
choices.b: No, because the leading question may be asked when there is a communication difficulty.
choices.c: No, because the question concerned the same subject matter as the direct examination of the employer.
choices.d: Yes, because the employer was being questioned by his own lawyer.
